# ultrarouter TypeScript SDK (@ultrarouter/sdk) 0.0.1 — full documentation

Every guide of this package concatenated in reading order, for AI agents (the generated API reference pages are linked, not inlined). The same files ship in the npm package and live at https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-typescript. Each file starts with a `<!-- file: path -->` marker.

<!-- file: README.md -->

# @ultrarouter/sdk

The official TypeScript SDK for ultrarouter, an OpenAI-compatible LLM
gateway and router. Send chat, streaming, tool-calling, structured-output and embedding requests
through the gateway with an `openai`-shaped client; read what every request cost and which model
served it; and use the ultrarouter resources (call types, evals, outcomes, preflight, Bench) from
typed methods.

- **OpenAI-shaped**: `chat.completions.create`, `embeddings.create`, `models.list`, plus
  `asOpenAI()` to keep using the official `openai` client.
- **Typed end to end**: request and response types are checked against the published OpenAPI
  document; `ur.request()` gives typed access to every operation in it.
- **Robust transport**: retries for retryable failures with backoff and `Retry-After`, a total
  timeout, `AbortSignal`, and idempotency keys on writes.
- **Zero runtime dependencies**: `fetch`-based; ESM and CommonJS; tested on Node.js 20+ and Deno 2,
  expected to work (not yet tested) on Bun and edge runtimes. See
  [runtimes](./docs/installation.md).
- **Batteries for CI**: the `ur` CLI and a GitHub Action for Bench and application-CI gates.

Version `0.0.1` is an early release; expect the API to evolve before 1.0.

## Install

<!-- doctest: skip — installs from the npm registry -->

```bash
npm install @ultrarouter/sdk
```

## Quickstart

Set your key and the URL of the gateway you run (there is no hosted default):

```bash
export ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY=ur_sk_test_...
export ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL=https://gateway.example.com   # required; or http://localhost:8080 for a local gateway
```

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter(); // reads ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY and ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL

const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Say hello in one word.' }],
});

console.log(res.choices[0]?.message.content);
console.log(res.ur.request_id, res.ur.model_served, res.ur.cost_usd);
```

Every response carries the `ur` block: the gateway request id, the model and provider that served
it, routing and compression details, and the cost. Model ids are provider-prefixed; the ones in
these docs are illustrative, and `ur.models.list()` shows what your gateway serves.

## Configuration

| Setting     | Option         | Environment                                | Default                      |
| ----------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| API key     | `apiKey`       | `ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY`, then `UR_API_KEY`   | required                     |
| Gateway URL | `baseURL`      | `ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL`, then `UR_BASE_URL` | required (no hosted default) |
| Model       | `defaultModel` |                                            | none                         |
| Retries     | `maxRetries`   |                                            | `2`                          |
| Timeout     | `timeout` (ms) |                                            | `600000`                     |

Also: request `defaults` (call type, compression, provider preferences, cost cap), the `autopilot`
intent, a Bench capture tag, `defaultHeaders`, a custom `fetch`, and durable outcome stores. See
[configuration](./docs/configuration.md).

## Feature tour

### Streaming

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });
const stream = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  stream: true,
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Write a haiku about rivers.' }],
});
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.choices[0]?.delta.content ?? '');
  if (chunk.ur) console.log(`\n(${chunk.ur.model_served}, $${String(chunk.ur.cost_usd)})`);
}
```

[Streaming guide](./docs/streaming.md)

### Tools and structured outputs

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });

const withTools = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'What is the weather in Oslo?' }],
  tools: [
    {
      type: 'function',
      function: {
        name: 'get_weather',
        parameters: {
          type: 'object',
          properties: { city: { type: 'string' } },
          required: ['city'],
        },
      },
    },
  ],
});
console.log(withTools.choices[0]?.message.tool_calls);

const structured = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Classify: "my parcel never arrived"' }],
  response_format: {
    type: 'json_schema',
    json_schema: {
      name: 'label',
      schema: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: { label: { type: 'string', enum: ['billing', 'shipping', 'other'] } },
        required: ['label'],
      },
    },
  },
});
console.log(JSON.parse(structured.choices[0]?.message.content ?? '{}'));
```

[Tools](./docs/tools.md) · [Structured outputs](./docs/structured-outputs.md)

### Embeddings and models

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const emb = await ur.embeddings.create({
  model: 'openai/text-embedding-3-small',
  input: ['first text', 'second text'],
});
console.log(emb.data.length, (emb.data[0]?.embedding as number[]).length);

const models = await ur.models.list({ capability: 'tools' });
const detail = await ur.models.retrieve('openai/gpt-5.2-mini');
console.log(models.data.length, detail.offers.length);
```

[Embeddings](./docs/embeddings.md) · [Models](./docs/models.md)

### Keep using the `openai` client

```ts
import OpenAI from 'openai';
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const openai = new UltraRouter().asOpenAI(OpenAI); // baseURL (+ /v1), key and headers preset
const res = await openai.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }],
});
console.log(res.choices[0]?.message.content);
```

[OpenAI compatibility](./docs/openai-compatibility.md)

### Native passthrough: the official OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs

The gateway forwards the OpenAI Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`) and the Anthropic Messages API
(`POST /v1/messages`) to the provider unchanged, metering each call. Point the official client at
your gateway with two environment variables (`OPENAI_BASE_URL=<gateway>/v1`,
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<gateway>`) and your `ur_sk_…` key — nothing else changes.

```ts
import OpenAI from 'openai';

// OPENAI_BASE_URL=<your gateway>/v1 and OPENAI_API_KEY=<your ur_sk_… key> point the official client here.
const openai = new OpenAI();
const res = await openai.responses.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  input: 'Give me one word for "fast".',
});
console.log(res.output_text);
```

[Native passthrough](./docs/passthrough.md)

### Errors and retries

Errors carry a stable `code`, the HTTP `status`, the `requestId` and a `retryable` flag. Retryable
failures (rate limits, provider outages, network errors) are retried automatically; non-retryable
ones, such as `model_unpriced` (a model with no price, refused before dispatch), fail immediately.

```ts
import UltraRouter, { ModelUnpricedError, isUltraRouterError } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ maxRetries: 2, timeout: 30_000 });
try {
  await ur.chat.completions.create({
    model: 'example/unpriced-model',
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }],
  });
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof ModelUnpricedError) console.log('choose a priced model');
  else if (isUltraRouterError(err)) console.log(err.code, err.status, err.requestId);
  else throw err;
}
```

[Errors](./docs/errors.md) · [Retries, timeouts and idempotency](./docs/retries-timeouts-idempotency.md)

### Any operation, typed

`ur.request()` reaches every operation in the published OpenAPI document with typed path
parameters, query, body and response, even those without a dedicated method:

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const key = await ur.request('get', '/v1/key');
const model = await ur.request('get', '/v1/models/{id}', { path: { id: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' } });
console.log(key.scopes, model.id);
```

[Typed requests](./docs/typed-requests.md) · [API coverage](./docs/api-coverage.md)

### Outcomes

Record what happened after a model call (a schema check passed, a human edited the draft, a claim
resolved) against the artifact it produced. Events are queued durably and replayed safely.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });
await ur.withArtifact('ticket-4821', async (scope) => {
  const res = await scope.chat.completions.create({
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Draft a reply to ticket 4821.' }],
  });
  console.log('id' in res ? res.ur.artifact_id : 'stream');
  await scope.record({ channel: 'mechanical', kind: 'schema_valid' });
}); // the outcome queue is flushed when the scope ends
```

[Outcomes](./docs/outcomes.md) · [Reviewer adapter](./docs/reviewer.md)

### Preflight: learned context without proxying

Calling your model provider directly? Ask the gateway first which model to use and which learned
context to inject, then insert it at the right position:

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const messages = [
  { role: 'system' as const, content: 'You answer customer questions.' },
  { role: 'user' as const, content: 'Where is order 4711?' },
];
const session = await ur.useLearned({ call_type: 'support-reply', messages });
const prompt = session.apply(messages); // send `prompt` to your provider
console.log(session.model, prompt.length);
```

[Preflight and learned context](./docs/preflight.md)

### Context runtime

`@ultrarouter/sdk/context` is a pure, network-free runtime for describing, compiling and auditing
the context of a model call. Lifting messages and turning them back round-trips byte for byte:

```ts
import { fromMessages, toMessages } from '@ultrarouter/sdk/context';

const messages = [
  { role: 'system' as const, content: 'You are a support assistant.' },
  { role: 'user' as const, content: 'Where is my order?' },
];
const lifted = fromMessages(messages);
console.log(lifted.labels.map((l) => l.kind));
console.log(JSON.stringify(toMessages(lifted.manifest)) === JSON.stringify(messages)); // true
```

[Context runtime](./docs/context-runtime.md)

### CLI and GitHub Action

The package ships the `ur` command for CI: Bench baseline-compare gates, application-CI checks with
a pull-request comment, outcome imports, and knowledge-pack validation. In a project that depends on the
package, run it with `npx ur`; without installing, name the package:
`npx --package=@ultrarouter/sdk@0.0.1 ur --help`.

```bash
npx ur --help
npx ur bench run support-replies --capture "npm test" --gate --baseline bench:main --budget 5
npx ur outcomes import outcomes.jsonl
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/bench.yml (excerpt)
- uses: lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-typescript@v0.0.1
  with:
    mode: bench
    suite: support-replies
    capture: npm test
    api-key: ${{ secrets.ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY }}
```

[CLI](./docs/cli.md) · [GitHub Action](./docs/github-action.md)

<!-- file: AGENTS.md -->

# AGENTS.md — using and changing `@ultrarouter/sdk`

This file is for AI coding agents (and humans who like short, exact instructions). It has two parts:
how to **use** the SDK in an application, and how to **work on** this repository.

## Part 1 — using the SDK

`@ultrarouter/sdk` is the official TypeScript client for ultrarouter, an OpenAI-compatible LLM
gateway and router. It mirrors the `openai` client (`chat.completions.create`, `embeddings.create`,
`models.list`) and adds ultrarouter resources under `ur.*`. Zero runtime dependencies, ESM and
CommonJS; tested on Node.js 20+ and Deno 2, expected to work (untested) on Bun and edge runtimes.

### Install and configure

<!-- doctest: skip — installs from the npm registry -->

```bash
npm install @ultrarouter/sdk
export ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY=ur_sk_test_...         # or UR_API_KEY
export ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL=https://gateway.example.com  # required; your deployment (or http://localhost:8080 locally)
```

### Canonical patterns

Create one client and reuse it. Model ids are provider-prefixed (`openai/gpt-5.2-mini`); the ids
your gateway serves come from `models.list()`.

```ts
import UltraRouter, { ModelUnpricedError, UltraRouterError } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });

// 1. Chat completion. Every response carries the `ur` block (request id, served model, cost).
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Give me one word for "fast".' }],
});
console.log(res.choices[0]?.message.content, res.ur.request_id);

// 2. Streaming: the last chunk carries `usage` and `ur`.
const stream = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  stream: true,
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Count to three.' }],
});
for await (const chunk of stream) process.stdout.write(chunk.choices[0]?.delta.content ?? '');
process.stdout.write('\n');

// 3. Errors are typed. Branch on `code`, never on the message text.
try {
  await ur.chat.completions.create({
    model: 'example/unpriced-model',
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }],
  });
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof ModelUnpricedError) console.log('choose a priced model');
  else if (err instanceof UltraRouterError) console.log(err.code, err.status, err.retryable);
  else throw err;
}
```

Use the official `openai` package unchanged by pointing it at the gateway:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'openai';
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const openai = new UltraRouter().asOpenAI(OpenAI);
const res = await openai.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }],
});
console.log(res.choices[0]?.message.content);
```

Call any API operation, fully typed, even when it has no dedicated method:

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const detail = await ur.request('get', '/v1/models/{id}', { path: { id: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' } });
console.log(detail.offers.length);
```

### Pitfalls

- **Keys are server-side secrets.** Never ship an API key to a browser; call the gateway from your
  server. Use `ur_sk_test_…` keys for tests and Bench capture.
- **Default import vs named import.** ESM: `import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk'` or
  `import { UltraRouter } from '@ultrarouter/sdk'`. CommonJS:
  `const { UltraRouter } = require('@ultrarouter/sdk')`.
- **The context runtime is a separate entry:** `import { compile } from '@ultrarouter/sdk/context'`.
- **Retries are automatic** for retryable errors only (`rate_limited`, `provider_unavailable`,
  `provider_timeout`, network errors, and 408/429/5xx without a gateway code). A stream is retried
  only on a retryable response before it opens. Set `maxRetries: 0` in tests.
- **`model_unpriced` (403)** means the gateway has no price for the model; it is never retried.
  Pick a priced model.
- **Outcomes are queued durably.** `ur.outcomes.record` does not throw for a delivery failure (only
  an `OutcomeStoreError` when its store cannot persist); a timeout, any 401/403/408/429/5xx, or an
  answer without a well-formed gateway envelope (an HTML 400 from a proxy) keeps the event queued.
  Only `invalid_request` / `not_found` / `conflict` in a well-formed envelope drops it
  (`isDefinitiveRejection`). Call `await ur.ur.outcomes.flush()` before your process exits (or use
  `withArtifact`, which flushes for you); replays reuse the event's identity and Idempotency-Key.
- **`preflight()` with per-request case modules needs `messages`;** otherwise the answer is
  `knowledge: null` with `knowledge_reason: "case_query_missing"`.
- **Do not invent methods.** If a method is not in `docs/api/sdk.md`, use `ur.request()` with the
  path from `docs/api-coverage.md`.

### Where the documentation lives

All of these ship inside the package (`node_modules/@ultrarouter/sdk/`) and live in the repository:

- `README.md` — overview and quickstart.
- `llms.txt` — an index of every guide; `llms-full.txt` — every guide concatenated.
- `docs/README.md` — the guide index; `docs/*.md` — one guide per topic.
- `docs/api/sdk.md`, `docs/api/context.md` — the complete API reference (generated).
- `docs/api-coverage.md` — every HTTP operation and the method that calls it.
- `docs/cli.md`, `docs/github-action.md` — the `ur` CLI and the GitHub Action.

## Part 2 — working on this repository

### Layout

```text
src/                  the SDK (client.ts, types.ts, errors.ts, http.ts, resources.ts, …)
src/cli/              the `ur` CLI (a separate bundle entry; Node-only code lives here)
src/context.ts        the @ultrarouter/sdk/context entry
src/context-runtime/  GENERATED: the vendored context runtime. Never edit by hand.
src/generated/        GENERATED by `npm run codegen` from openapi/openapi.yaml (gitignored)
openapi/openapi.yaml  the synced API specification (two-line header + byte-identical body)
test/                 unit tests (vitest); test/support/mock-gateway.mjs is the local mock gateway
contract-tests/       hermetic batteries that drive the BUILT package and CLI as a user would
examples/             runnable example programs (executed by `npm run examples` against the mock gateway)
docs/                 guides; docs/api/ and docs/api-coverage.md are GENERATED
scripts/              build, docs, doctest, smoke, leak-scan and spec tooling
action.yml            the GitHub Action
```

### Commands

<!-- doctest: skip — the contributor commands; `npm run check` runs them all, in this order -->

```bash
npm ci                 # install (Node 20+)
npm run codegen        # regenerate src/generated/types.ts from openapi/openapi.yaml
npm run typecheck      # tsc: src, tests, the context entry, examples
npm test               # vitest unit suite
npm run build          # tsup: ESM + CJS + .d.ts, plus the CLI bundle
npm run contract       # hermetic batteries against the built package (needs build)
npm run doctest        # type-check + run the TS/JS blocks and the CLI shell blocks in README, AGENTS.md, docs/ (needs build)
npm run examples       # run every example against the mock gateway (needs build)
npm run docs:gen       # regenerate docs/api/*, docs/api-coverage.md, llms.txt, llms-full.txt
npm run docs:check     # fail if generated docs are stale; forbidden-claim lint
npm run size           # bundle size budgets
npm run smoke          # npm pack → install into a temp consumer → ESM/CJS/tsc/CLI/npx/OpenAI (+ Deno) checks
npm run leak-scan      # secrets, local paths, secret files in the tree + full git history + npm tarball
npm run check          # all of the above, in order (the gate; the ci workflow runs the same list on manual dispatch)
npm run test:integration  # against a REAL gateway; skipped unless ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY + ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL are set
```

### Rules

- `openapi/openapi.yaml` is synced, never hand-edited: `node scripts/openapi-sync.mjs <spec>` then
  `npm run codegen`. `npm run spec:check` verifies the header hash.
- `src/context-runtime/**` is generated by the gateway project's vendoring tool; never edit it. To
  document an undocumented export, add a documented re-export in `src/context.ts`.
- Every public export needs TSDoc, and every member of an SDK-authored exported interface or class
  too (`test/tsdoc.test.ts`). Then run `npm run docs:gen`.
- A new API operation: add a typed method (or rely on `ur.request()`), add it to
  `scripts/lib/coverage-map.mjs` with the test that proves it (`test/coverage-map.test.ts` enforces
  this), document it, and regenerate the docs.
- Every ``ts block in the docs must be a complete program that passes `npm run doctest`, and every
``bash block must run in the doctest sandbox (`test/doctest/sandbox/`, with `ur` and `npx` bound
  to the built CLI). Opting out needs `<!-- doctest: skip — reason -->` right above the block; a
  block that is meant to fail declares it with `<!-- doctest: exit <n> — reason -->`.
- No savings or performance claims in docs (`npm run docs:check`), and no secret, local path or
  secret file in the tree, the history or the tarball (`npm run leak-scan`; extra patterns can be
  supplied with `--patterns-file` or `ULTRAROUTER_LEAK_PATTERNS_FILE`).
- Never interpolate `${{ … }}` into a `run:` script in `action.yml` or the workflows: pass values
  through `env:` (`test/action.test.ts` enforces it), and pin third-party actions to commit SHAs.
- Zero runtime dependencies: anything the SDK needs at runtime is bundled or written here.
- `test/fixtures/queue-retention-cases.json` pins the durable-queue retention rules case by case and
  is shared byte-for-byte with the Python SDK (`test/queue-retention-fixture.test.ts` runs every
  case). A rule change edits the file in both SDKs together, never one alone.

# @ultrarouter/sdk documentation

Guides for the TypeScript SDK of ultrarouter, an OpenAI-compatible LLM
gateway and router. Every TypeScript example in these guides is a complete program that is
type-checked and executed in CI against a local mock gateway.

New here? Read [installation](./installation.md), then [configuration](./configuration.md), then
[chat completions](./chat-completions.md).

## Getting started

| Guide                                          | What it covers                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Installation and runtimes](./installation.md) | Install; ESM and CommonJS; supported runtimes (Node.js, Deno; Bun and edge untested); entry points; TypeScript setup.              |
| [Configuration](./configuration.md)            | Every constructor option, environment variables, base URL and self-hosting, defaults, Autopilot intent, Bench tag, custom `fetch`. |

## Model calls

| Guide                                             | What it covers                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Chat completions](./chat-completions.md)         | Parameters, ultrarouter extensions (`call_type`, `router`, `compression`, `models`, `ur.*`), reasoning, cache breakpoints, the `ur` response block.                     |
| [Streaming](./streaming.md)                       | `for await` streams, the final chunk, stopping early, mid-stream errors.                                                                                                |
| [Tools](./tools.md)                               | Function calling round trip, `tool_choice`, streamed tool calls.                                                                                                        |
| [Structured outputs](./structured-outputs.md)     | `json_schema` and `json_object`, capability errors.                                                                                                                     |
| [Embeddings](./embeddings.md)                     | Batches, base64 output, `dimensions`.                                                                                                                                   |
| [Models](./models.md)                             | `models.list` filters, `models.retrieve` offers, pricing and provenance fields.                                                                                         |

| [Native passthrough](./passthrough.md)            | The official OpenAI (Responses) and Anthropic (Messages) SDKs through your gateway: base URLs, key placement, the ultrarouter request/response headers, `ur.request()`. |

## Command line and CI

| Guide                               | What it covers                                                     |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [The `ur` CLI](./cli.md)            | Every command, flag, environment variable and exit code.           |
| [GitHub Action](./github-action.md) | Every mode, input and output, and the least-privilege permissions. |

## Runnable examples

[`examples/`](../examples/README.md) holds complete programs for the main flows. Each runs against
a real gateway with `ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY` set, and against the local mock in CI.

## For AI agents

Start with [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) for canonical patterns and pitfalls. [`llms.txt`](../llms.txt)
indexes these guides and [`llms-full.txt`](../llms-full.txt) contains all of them in one file. All
three ship inside the npm package, under `node_modules/@ultrarouter/sdk/`.

<!-- file: docs/installation.md -->

# Installation and runtimes

`@ultrarouter/sdk` has zero runtime dependencies and talks to the gateway with the platform
`fetch`. It ships ESM and CommonJS builds with TypeScript declarations.

| Runtime                                         | Support                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Node.js 20, 22, 24                              | Supported and tested in CI (every check, on each version).                                                                                                                                       |
| Deno 2                                          | Supported and tested in CI: the pack smoke runs the installed package under Deno (chat, streaming, embeddings, typed errors, the context entry).                                                 |
| Bun                                             | Expected to work (the client uses only `fetch`, `AbortController`, `TextDecoder` and `crypto`, and Bun runs Node.js packages), but no automated test runs on Bun.                                |
| Edge runtimes (Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge) | Expected to work for the client (Web APIs only), but no automated test runs on an edge runtime. The context entry and `FileOutcomeStore` need Node.js APIs; see [edge runtimes](#edge-runtimes). |

## Install

<!-- doctest: skip — installs from the npm registry -->

```bash
npm install @ultrarouter/sdk
# or
pnpm add @ultrarouter/sdk
yarn add @ultrarouter/sdk
bun add @ultrarouter/sdk
```

Then set your key:

```bash
export ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY=ur_sk_test_...
```

## ES modules

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello from ESM' }],
});
console.log(res.choices[0]?.message.content);
```

Named imports work too: `import { UltraRouter, UltraRouterError } from '@ultrarouter/sdk'`.

## CommonJS

`require()` returns the module namespace. Use the named `UltraRouter` export (the default export is
also available as `.default`):

```js
const { UltraRouter, UltraRouterError } = require('@ultrarouter/sdk');

const ur = new UltraRouter();
ur.chat.completions
  .create({ model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello from CJS' }] })
  .then((res) => console.log(res.choices[0].message.content))
  .catch((err) => {
    if (err instanceof UltraRouterError) console.error(err.code);
    process.exitCode = 1;
  });
```

## Entry points

| Import                     | Contents                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `@ultrarouter/sdk`         | The `UltraRouter` client, every request/response type, errors, and the pure helpers.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `@ultrarouter/sdk/context` | The pure context runtime (modules, contracts, `compile`, `fromMessages` / `toMessages`), knowledge packs, the learned-module placement rule and the hosted-prompt renderer. No network. See [context runtime](./context-runtime.md). |
| `ur` (binary)              | The command-line tool for CI gates and outcome imports. Node.js only. See [CLI](./cli.md).                                                                                                                                           |

Importing the client never loads the context runtime, and the reverse.

## Node.js

Node.js 20 or later. Everything works, including `FileOutcomeStore` (durable outcome queue on disk)
and the `ur` CLI:

```bash
npx ur --version
```

## Bun

Bun runs the same code as Node.js, ESM or CommonJS. Bun is not covered by the automated tests; report
anything that behaves differently there.

<!-- doctest: skip — needs Bun and installs from the npm registry -->

```bash
bun add @ultrarouter/sdk
ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY=ur_sk_test_... bun run app.ts
```

## Deno

Import through the `npm:` specifier and grant network and environment access:

<!-- doctest: skip — Deno-only `npm:` import specifier; the same code runs under Node.js in the ES modules section above -->

```ts
import UltraRouter from 'npm:@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello from Deno' }],
});
console.log(res.choices[0]?.message.content);
```

<!-- doctest: skip — needs Deno; the pack smoke runs the built package under Deno when it is installed -->

```bash
deno run --allow-net --allow-env main.ts
```

## Edge runtimes

The client needs only `fetch`, `AbortController`, `TextDecoder` and `crypto`, so it is designed to
run on edge runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers or Vercel Edge Functions; no automated test runs on
one yet. Edge runtimes usually have no `process.env`, so pass the key and base URL explicitly:

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

interface Env {
  ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY: string;
  ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL?: string;
}

// A Cloudflare Workers-style module: the platform calls `fetch(request, env)`.
export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
    const ur = new UltraRouter({
      apiKey: env.ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY,
      ...(env.ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL !== undefined ? { baseURL: env.ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL } : {}),
    });
    const { question } = (await request.json()) as { question: string };
    const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
      model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
      messages: [{ role: 'user', content: question }],
    });
    return Response.json({ answer: res.choices[0]?.message.content ?? '' });
  },
};
```

Not available on edge runtimes: `FileOutcomeStore` (it needs `node:fs`; use the default
`MemoryOutcomeStore` or your own `OutcomeStore`) and the `ur` CLI. The `@ultrarouter/sdk/context`
entry uses `node:crypto` for sha256; it runs where `node:crypto` is available (Node.js, Bun, Deno,
and edge runtimes with Node.js compatibility enabled).

## Browsers

The SDK works in a browser bundle, but do not ship an API key to browsers: anyone who loads the
page can read it. Call the gateway from your server and expose your own endpoint instead.

## TypeScript

Types are bundled; no `@types` package is needed. TypeScript 5 or later is recommended. To resolve
the `@ultrarouter/sdk/context` subpath, use `"moduleResolution": "bundler"`, `"node16"` or
`"nodenext"` (the older `"node"` resolution cannot read package `exports`). The types are written
for `strict` mode.

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "strict": true
  }
}
```

## Verify the install

```ts
import UltraRouter, { VERSION } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const key = await ur.ur.key.get();
console.log(`@ultrarouter/sdk ${VERSION} → ${ur.baseURL} (key mode: ${key.mode})`);
```

## Related

- [Configuration](./configuration.md) · [Troubleshooting](./troubleshooting.md)
- [Context runtime](./context-runtime.md) · [CLI](./cli.md)

<!-- file: docs/configuration.md -->

# Configuration

Everything about a client is set when you construct it, and every request-shaping setting can be
overridden per call. With the two environment variables set, `new UltraRouter()` needs no
arguments at all.

## Environment variables

| Variable                                     | Used for            | Notes                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY` (or `UR_API_KEY`)      | The API key         | Required unless you pass `apiKey`. `ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY` wins when both are set.                               |
| `ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL` (or `UR_BASE_URL`)    | The gateway URL     | Required unless you pass `baseURL`; there is no hosted default. `ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL` wins when both are set. |
| `UR_BENCH`, `UR_BENCH_RUN`, `UR_BENCH_TRACE` | A Bench capture tag | Optional; used when the `bench` option is not passed. See [Bench](./bench.md).                                 |

Precedence for each setting is: the constructor option, then `ULTRAROUTER_*`, then `UR_*`, then the
built-in default where there is one. The API key and the base URL have no default — they are
required, and construction throws when neither the option nor an environment variable supplies them.
Empty environment variables count as unset. The `ur` CLI reads the same variables (and its
`--api-key` / `--base-url` flags win over them).

```bash
export ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY=ur_sk_test_...
export ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL=https://gateway.example.com   # required: your own deployment (or http://localhost:8080 locally)
```

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter(); // reads the environment
console.log(ur.baseURL);
```

## API keys

Keys look like `ur_sk_live_…` (live traffic) or `ur_sk_test_…` (test traffic). A key has scopes
that decide which routes it may call (for example `gateway:invoke` for chat, `config:write` to
change call types, `outcomes:write` for outcomes). Inspect the key a client uses with
`ur.ur.key.get()`:

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const key = await ur.ur.key.get();
console.log(key.mode, key.scopes, key.workspace_id);
```

Keep keys on the server. The SDK can run in a browser, but a key embedded in browser code is
readable by anyone who loads the page.

## Base URL and self-hosting

`baseURL` is the gateway origin without `/v1`; trailing slashes are removed. Point it at any
deployment of the gateway, for example one you run yourself or a staging environment:

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({
  apiKey: process.env.ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY,
  baseURL: process.env.ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL, // e.g. https://gateway.example.com, or http://localhost:8080
});
console.log(ur.baseURL);
```

## All constructor options

| Option           | Type                                | Default                                                                  | Meaning                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apiKey`         | `string`                            | `ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY`, then `UR_API_KEY`                                 | The API key. Construction throws `authentication` when none is found.                   |
| `baseURL`        | `string`                            | `ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL`, then `UR_BASE_URL` (required; no hosted default) | The gateway URL, without `/v1`. Construction throws `configuration` when none is found. |
| `defaultModel`   | `string`                            | none                                                                     | Used when a chat or embeddings call omits `model`.                                      |
| `defaults`       | `UltraRouterDefaults`               | `{}`                                                                     | Request defaults, each overridable per call (below).                                    |
| `autopilot`      | `'audit' \| 'recommend' \| 'auto'`  | none                                                                     | The one-line routing intent (below).                                                    |
| `bench`          | `string \| { suite, run?, trace? }` | `UR_BENCH*` env                                                          | A Bench capture tag stamped on every request (below).                                   |
| `timeout`        | `number` (ms)                       | `600000`                                                                 | Total time per call: retries and reading the body (a whole stream).                     |
| `maxRetries`     | `number`                            | `2`                                                                      | Retries for retryable failures.                                                         |
| `fetch`          | `FetchLike`                         | `globalThis.fetch`                                                       | A custom `fetch` (tests, proxies, instrumentation).                                     |
| `defaultHeaders` | `Record<string, string>`            | `{}`                                                                     | Headers sent on every request (per-call `headers` win).                                 |
| `outcomeStore`   | `OutcomeStore`                      | `MemoryOutcomeStore`                                                     | Where outcome events are persisted before they are sent.                                |
| `reviewerStore`  | `OutcomeStore<QueuedReviewerEvent>` | `MemoryOutcomeStore`                                                     | Where reviewer events are persisted before they are sent.                               |
| `preflightCache` | `{ maxEntries?: number }`           | `{ maxEntries: 1000 }`                                                   | The bound on the `preflight()` cache (LRU); `0` turns it off.                           |

## Request defaults and per-call precedence

`defaultModel` and `defaults` set values for every call. A per-call value always wins; an omitted
per-call value falls back to the default.

| Default                | Applies to       | Sent as                                               |
| ---------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `defaultModel`         | chat, embeddings | `model`                                               |
| `defaults.router`      | chat             | `router`                                              |
| `defaults.compression` | chat             | `compression`                                         |
| `defaults.callType`    | chat, embeddings | `call_type`                                           |
| `defaults.provider`    | chat             | `provider`                                            |
| `defaults.maxCostUsd`  | chat, embeddings | `ur.max_cost_usd` (a per-call `ur.max_cost_usd` wins) |

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({
  defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  defaults: {
    callType: 'support-reply',
    compression: 'off',
    provider: { sort: 'price' },
    maxCostUsd: 0.02,
  },
});

// Uses every default.
const a = await ur.chat.completions.create({ messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hi' }] });
// Overrides the model and the call type for this call only.
const b = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6',
  call_type: 'escalation',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hi' }],
});
console.log(a.model, b.model);
```

## Autopilot intent

`autopilot` is a single intent setting that maps onto the request `router` field:

| `autopilot`   | Sends                  | Meaning                                                   |
| ------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `'audit'`     | `router: 'off'`        | Observe only; serve the requested model.                  |
| `'recommend'` | `router: 'candidates'` | Rank approved candidate models.                           |
| `'auto'`      | `router: 'auto'`       | Let the router act once the gateway's evidence qualifies. |

The setting is a ceiling: a per-call `router` may lower autonomy (for example `off` on a client
set to `auto`) but a higher value is clamped down to the ceiling. `auto` is an intent, not a
bypass; the gateway still decides when routing is allowed. Omit `autopilot` for a plain
pass-through client. `ur.ur.autopilot.status()` reads the read-only readiness rollup.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ autopilot: 'recommend', defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });

const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  router: 'auto', // clamped to 'candidates' by the 'recommend' ceiling
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello' }],
});
console.log(ur.ur.autopilot.mode, res.ur.routing.mode);

const readiness = await ur.ur.autopilot.status();
console.log(readiness.state, readiness.total_requests);
```

## Bench capture tag

`bench` tags every request for a Bench suite by stamping `X-UR-Bench-Suite`, `X-UR-Bench-Run` and
`X-UR-Bench-Trace` headers (they also ride `asOpenAI()` clients). `trace` may be a function, called
per request. A per-call `bench` field overrides the client tag. Bench capture needs a test key
(`ur_sk_test_…`); with a live key the SDK warns once and the gateway refuses the capture unless your
workspace allows live capture. See [Bench](./bench.md).

```ts
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({
  bench: { suite: 'support-replies', run: 'nightly', trace: () => randomUUID() },
});
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello' }],
});
console.log(res.ur.request_id);
```

## Custom fetch and default headers

Pass your own `fetch` to add logging, route through a proxy agent, or fake the gateway in tests:

```ts
import UltraRouter, { type FetchLike } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const logged: FetchLike = async (input, init) => {
  const started = Date.now();
  const res = await fetch(input, init);
  console.log(
    init?.method ?? 'GET',
    String(input),
    res.status,
    `${String(Date.now() - started)}ms`,
  );
  return res;
};

const ur = new UltraRouter({ fetch: logged, defaultHeaders: { 'x-app-version': '1.4.0' } });
await ur.models.list();
```

## Outcome and reviewer stores

Outcome events (`ur.ur.outcomes.record`) and reviewer decisions (`ur.ur.reviewer.record`) are
persisted before they are sent and replayed on retry. The default `MemoryOutcomeStore` lasts for
the life of the process; `FileOutcomeStore(path)` (Node.js only) survives restarts:

```ts
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import UltraRouter, { FileOutcomeStore } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({
  outcomeStore: new FileOutcomeStore(join(tmpdir(), 'ur-outcomes.json')),
});
const report = await ur.ur.outcomes.flush(); // send anything left over from a previous run
console.log(report.delivered, report.pending);
```

See [outcomes](./outcomes.md) and [the reviewer adapter](./reviewer.md).
