- [Installation and runtimes](./installation.md)
- [Retries, timeouts and idempotency](./retries-timeouts-idempotency.md)
- [OpenAI compatibility](./openai-compatibility.md)

<!-- file: docs/chat-completions.md -->

# Chat completions

`ur.chat.completions.create(params, options?)` sends a chat request through the gateway
(`POST /v1/chat/completions`). The request and response follow the OpenAI chat-completions shape,
with a few ultrarouter fields added: request-level routing and compression controls, a stable call
type, and the `ur` block on every response (the request id, the model that served, the cost).

Model ids are provider-prefixed (`openai/gpt-5.2-mini`). The ids in these docs are illustrative:
which models you can use depends on your gateway, and `ur.models.list()` tells you.

## A minimal call

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  messages: [
    { role: 'system', content: 'Answer in one short sentence.' },
    { role: 'user', content: 'What is the capital of France?' },
  ],
  temperature: 0.2,
  max_completion_tokens: 100,
});

console.log(res.choices[0]?.message.content);
console.log(res.usage.total_tokens, res.ur.cost_usd, res.ur.model_served);
```

Set `defaultModel` on the client to omit `model` from each call (a per-call `model` still wins):

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({ messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hi!' }] });
console.log(res.model);
```

## OpenAI parameters

| Parameter                               | Notes                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `model`                                 | Provider-prefixed id. Optional when the client has `defaultModel`.                               |
| `messages`                              | `system`, `developer`, `user`, `assistant` and `tool` messages.                                  |
| `temperature`, `top_p`, `seed`          | Sampling controls.                                                                               |
| `max_completion_tokens`, `max_tokens`   | Output cap (`max_tokens` is the legacy name).                                                    |
| `stop`, `n`                             | Stop sequences; number of choices.                                                               |
| `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty` | Repetition penalties.                                                                            |
| `logprobs`, `top_logprobs`              | Log probabilities.                                                                               |
| `tools`, `tool_choice`                  | Function calling. See [tools](./tools.md).                                                       |
| `response_format`                       | `json_object` or `json_schema`. See [structured outputs](./structured-outputs.md).               |
| `stream`, `stream_options`              | Server-sent events. See [streaming](./streaming.md).                                             |
| `reasoning_effort`                      | `none` \| `minimal` \| `low` \| `medium` \| `high`.                                              |
| `reasoning`                             | OpenRouter-style `{ effort?, max_tokens?, exclude? }`; takes precedence over `reasoning_effort`. |
| `user`, `metadata`                      | An end-user id; free-form metadata.                                                              |

### Reasoning

`reasoning_effort` is forwarded to providers that support it and mapped to a thinking-token budget
for providers that use budgets. A model with no reasoning control is refused with
`capability_unsupported` rather than silently ignoring the setting.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2',
  reasoning_effort: 'low',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Is 221 prime? Answer yes or no.' }],
});
console.log(res.choices[0]?.message.content);
```

### Multi-part content and cache breakpoints

`content` may be an array of parts. A part can carry `cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }` to mark
a prompt-cache breakpoint; providers with explicit cache breakpoints honour it, others ignore it.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const policy = 'Refunds are accepted within 30 days of delivery with a receipt.';

const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6',
  messages: [
    {
      role: 'system',
      content: [{ type: 'text', text: policy, cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral', ttl: '5m' } }],
    },
    { role: 'user', content: 'Can I return a jacket I bought last week?' },
  ],
});
console.log(res.usage.prompt_tokens_details?.cached_tokens ?? 0, 'cached input tokens');
```

## ultrarouter parameters

| Parameter     | Type                                                            | Notes                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `call_type`   | `string`                                                        | A stable slug naming this kind of request (`support-reply`). Groups requests for evaluation and routing. See [call types](./call-types.md). |
| `models`      | `string[]`                                                      | Ordered fallback models, tried when the primary fails.                                                                                      |
| `router`      | `'off' \| 'auto' \| 'candidates'`                               | Routing mode for this call. `off` serves the requested model.                                                                               |
| `compression` | mode string or `{ mode, no_compress_fields, max_quality_risk }` | Prompt compression control. `off` is the default.                                                                                           |
| `provider`    | `ProviderPreferences`                                           | OpenRouter-style provider preferences: `order`, `allow_fallbacks`, `ignore`, `sort`, …                                                      |
| `ur`          | `UrRequestOptions`                                              | Per-request controls; see below.                                                                                                            |
| `bench`       | `string \| { suite, run?, trace? }`                             | Tag this call for a Bench suite. See [Bench](./bench.md).                                                                                   |

Compression modes are `off`, `semantic_safe` and `adaptive`.
The legacy values `lossless` and `auto` are deprecated aliases that still parse (the legacy `lossless` alias is not a guarantee that the model sees identical text).

### The `ur` request options

| Field             | Type                                      | Notes                                                                                       |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `max_cost_usd`    | `number`                                  | Refuse the call before dispatch (`max_cost_exceeded`) when its estimated cost exceeds this. |
| `trace_id`        | `string`                                  | Your trace id, grouping related requests.                                                   |
| `tags`            | `Record<string, string>`                  | Free-form tags recorded with the request.                                                   |
| `timeout_ms`      | `number`                                  | An upstream timeout for this request.                                                       |
| `segments`        | `{ index, kind }[]`                       | Label messages (`reference_context`, `history`, …) to guide compression segmentation.       |
| `artifact`        | `string`                                  | The artifact key this request contributes to. See [outcomes](./outcomes.md).                |
| `situation`       | `Record<string, unknown>`                 | Declared situation facets (labels and values only).                                         |
| `manifest`        | `UrManifest`                              | A declared context manifest from `toWire()`. See [context runtime](./context-runtime.md).   |
| `context_modules` | `{ module_id, module_version }[]`         | Learned-context modules pinned to exact versions (at most 8).                               |
| `prompt_vars`     | `Record<string, string\|number\|boolean>` | Values for the active hosted prompt's `{{variables}}`. See [call types](./call-types.md).   |
| `bench`           | Bench tag                                 | Same as the top-level `bench` (the top-level one is folded in here).                        |

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  models: ['anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6'], // fallback
  call_type: 'support-reply',
  router: 'off',
  compression: { mode: 'off' },
  provider: { sort: 'price', allow_fallbacks: true },
  ur: {
    max_cost_usd: 0.05,
    trace_id: 'ticket-4821',
    tags: { team: 'support' },
  },
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Where is my order?' }],
});

console.log(res.ur.call_type, res.ur.routing.fallback_used);
```

## The response

The response is an OpenAI `chat.completion` object plus `ur`:

| Field                              | Meaning                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`, `object`, `created`, `model` | The completion identity.                                                                      |
| `choices[].message`                | `role`, `content`, and `tool_calls` when the model calls tools.                               |
| `choices[].finish_reason`          | `stop`, `length`, `tool_calls`, …                                                             |
| `usage`                            | `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens`, `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`.  |
| `ur.request_id`                    | The gateway request id. Use it with `ur.ur.generation.get()` and `ur.ur.requests.feedback()`. |
| `ur.call_type`                     | The call type the request was attributed to, or `null`.                                       |
| `ur.model_served`, `ur.provider`   | Which model and provider actually served the request.                                         |
| `ur.routing`                       | `{ mode, fallback_used, engine? }`.                                                           |
| `ur.compression`                   | What compression did (`applied`, and estimates labelled by `savings_basis`).                  |
| `ur.cost_usd`                      | The request cost in USD.                                                                      |
| `ur.byok`                          | Whether your own provider key served the request.                                             |
| `ur.artifact_id`                   | Present when the request declared an artifact.                                                |
| `ur.bench`                         | Present on a Bench-tagged request (the capture is `queued`).                                  |
| `ur.verified_memory`               | Present only when the answer came from the workspace's verified memory instead of a provider. |

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello' }],
});

// Look the request up later, and rate it.
const stats = await ur.ur.generation.get(res.ur.request_id);
console.log(stats.tokens.total, stats.cost.total_usd, stats.timing.latency_ms);
await ur.ur.requests.feedback(res.ur.request_id, { rating: 1, tags: ['helpful'] });
```

## Pitfalls

- A request without `model` and without a client `defaultModel` is rejected by the gateway with
  `invalid_request`.
- `ur.max_cost_usd` is a pre-dispatch estimate check, not a billing guarantee.
- The `ur` request field is the per-request extension object; `ur.ur.*` on the client is the
  resource namespace. They are unrelated.
- Model capabilities differ: a model without tools or `json_schema` support is refused with
  `capability_unsupported`.

## Related

- [Streaming](./streaming.md) · [Tools](./tools.md) · [Structured outputs](./structured-outputs.md)
- [Configuration](./configuration.md) · [Errors](./errors.md)
- [Feedback and generation stats](./feedback-and-generation.md)

<!-- file: docs/streaming.md -->

# Streaming

Pass `stream: true` to `ur.chat.completions.create()` and you get an async iterable of
`chat.completion.chunk` objects instead of a completion. Iterate it with `for await`. The final
chunk carries `usage` and the ultrarouter `ur` block (request id, model served, cost).

The parser uses only `fetch`, `ReadableStream` and `TextDecoder`, so streaming works on Node.js,
Bun, Deno and edge runtimes.

## Print a reply as it arrives

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

const stream = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  stream: true,
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Count from one to five.' }],
});

let text = '';
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  const delta = chunk.choices[0]?.delta.content ?? '';
  text += delta;
  process.stdout.write(delta);
  if (chunk.ur !== undefined) {
    // The final chunk: usage and the `ur` block.
    console.log(`\n${String(chunk.usage?.total_tokens)} tokens, $${String(chunk.ur.cost_usd)}`);
  }
}
console.log(text.length > 0);
```

## What the chunks contain

| Field                         | Meaning                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `choices[0].delta.role`       | On the first chunk: `assistant`.                                |
| `choices[0].delta.content`    | The next piece of text (may be empty).                          |
| `choices[0].delta.tool_calls` | Tool-call fragments when the model calls tools.                 |
| `choices[0].finish_reason`    | Set on the last content chunk (`stop`, `length`, `tool_calls`). |
| `usage`                       | Token usage, on the final chunk.                                |
| `ur`                          | The ultrarouter response block, on the final chunk.             |

Heartbeat comment lines and the terminating `data: [DONE]` frame are handled by the SDK; you never
see them.

## Collect the whole reply

```ts
import UltraRouter, { type ChatCompletionStream } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

async function collect(
  stream: ChatCompletionStream,
): Promise<{ text: string; requestId?: string }> {
  let text = '';
  let requestId: string | undefined;
  for await (const chunk of stream) {
    text += chunk.choices[0]?.delta.content ?? '';
    if (chunk.ur !== undefined) requestId = chunk.ur.request_id;
  }
  return requestId === undefined ? { text } : { text, requestId };
}

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });
const result = await collect(
  await ur.chat.completions.create({ stream: true, messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hi' }] }),
);
console.log(result);
```

## Stop early

Breaking out of the `for await` loop releases the stream and cancels the underlying request. To
cancel from elsewhere (a user pressing "stop"), pass an `AbortSignal`:

```ts
import UltraRouter, { isUltraRouterError } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const controller = new AbortController();

const stream = await ur.chat.completions.create(
  {
    model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
    stream: true,
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Tell me a long story.' }],
  },
  { signal: controller.signal },
);

let received = 0;
try {
  for await (const chunk of stream) {
    received += (chunk.choices[0]?.delta.content ?? '').length;
    break; // stop after the first chunk
  }
} catch (err) {
  if (!isUltraRouterError(err)) throw err;
}
console.log(`stopped after ${String(received)} characters`);
```

## Errors

- A request that fails **before** the stream opens (bad key, unknown model, `model_unpriced`)
  rejects the `create()` call with an `UltraRouterError`, just like a non-streaming call.
- A failure **after** the stream opened arrives as an `event: error` frame; the `for await` loop
  throws an `UltraRouterError` with that frame's `code` (its `status` is `0`, because the HTTP
  status was already 200). The SDK never silently truncates a stream.
- A malformed frame throws an `UltraRouterError` with code `internal`.
- A stream that ends before the gateway's `data: [DONE]` throws an `UltraRouterError` with code
  `connection`: the response is incomplete, so it is never reported as a clean finish.
- The total `timeout` and your `AbortSignal` keep applying while chunks arrive: a stream that stalls
  or outlives the deadline throws `timeout`, an abort throws `aborted`. See
  [timeouts](./retries-timeouts-idempotency.md#timeouts-and-cancellation).
- The parser follows the Server-Sent Events standard: lines may end in LF, CRLF or CR (also split
  across network chunks), `:` lines are comments, and unknown fields are ignored, so a proxy that
  rewrites line endings does not break a stream.
- A stream carries no idempotency key. It is retried only when the gateway answers with a
  retryable error **before** the stream opens (nothing was generated); never after a network
  failure, and never once chunks have started. If a stream fails partway, decide in your
  application whether to start a new request.

```ts
import UltraRouter, { ModelUnpricedError } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
try {
  const stream = await ur.chat.completions.create({
    model: 'example/unpriced-model',
    stream: true,
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }],
  });
  for await (const chunk of stream) process.stdout.write(chunk.choices[0]?.delta.content ?? '');
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof ModelUnpricedError) console.log('refused before the stream opened:', err.code);
  else throw err;
}
```

## With the OpenAI client

`ur.asOpenAI(OpenAI)` returns an `openai` client pointed at the gateway; its streaming works the
same way. See [OpenAI compatibility](./openai-compatibility.md).

## Related

- [Chat completions](./chat-completions.md)
- [Retries, timeouts and idempotency](./retries-timeouts-idempotency.md)
- [Errors](./errors.md)

<!-- file: docs/tools.md -->

# Tools (function calling)

Tools let the model ask your code to do something: look up an order, call an API, run a query.
You describe each tool with a JSON Schema; the model replies with `tool_calls` instead of text; you
run the tools and send their results back as `tool` messages; the model then answers. The request
and response shapes are the OpenAI ones.

## The full round trip

```ts
import UltraRouter, { type ChatMessage } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });

const tools = [
  {
    type: 'function',
    function: {
      name: 'get_weather',
      description: 'Current weather for a city.',
      parameters: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: { city: { type: 'string' }, unit: { type: 'string', enum: ['c', 'f'] } },
        required: ['city'],
      },
    },
  },
];

interface ToolCall {
  id: string;
  type: 'function';
  function: { name: string; arguments: string };
}

const messages: ChatMessage[] = [{ role: 'user', content: 'Is it cold in Oslo right now?' }];
const first = await ur.chat.completions.create({ messages, tools, tool_choice: 'auto' });
const assistant = first.choices[0]?.message;
const calls = (assistant?.tool_calls ?? []) as ToolCall[];

if (calls.length > 0) {
  // Keep the assistant turn that asked for the tools, then answer each call.
  messages.push({ role: 'assistant', content: assistant?.content ?? null, tool_calls: calls });
  for (const call of calls) {
    const args = JSON.parse(call.function.arguments) as { city: string };
    const result = { city: args.city, temperature_c: -3 }; // your real tool runs here
    messages.push({ role: 'tool', tool_call_id: call.id, content: JSON.stringify(result) });
  }
  const final = await ur.chat.completions.create({ messages, tools });
  console.log(final.choices[0]?.message.content);
} else {
  console.log(assistant?.content);
}
```

## Choosing how tools are used

| `tool_choice`                                             | Effect                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `'auto'` (default when tools are present)                 | The model decides.                     |
| `'none'`                                                  | The model answers in text.             |
| `'required'`                                              | The model must call at least one tool. |
| `{ type: 'function', function: { name: 'get_weather' } }` | The model must call that tool.         |

## Parsing arguments safely

`function.arguments` is a JSON string produced by the model. Parse it inside `try`/`catch` and
validate it (with your own checks or a schema library) before acting on it; the model can produce
arguments that are valid JSON but not what you expect.

## Streaming tool calls

With `stream: true`, tool calls arrive as fragments in `choices[0].delta.tool_calls`. Accumulate
them by `index` until the chunk whose `finish_reason` is `tool_calls`:

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });
const stream = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  stream: true,
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Weather in Lima?' }],
  tools: [
    {
      type: 'function',
      function: {
        name: 'get_weather',
        parameters: { type: 'object', properties: { city: { type: 'string' } } },
      },
    },
  ],
});

interface Fragment {
  index: number;
  id?: string;
  function?: { name?: string; arguments?: string };
}
const calls = new Map<number, { id: string; name: string; arguments: string }>();
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  for (const frag of (chunk.choices[0]?.delta.tool_calls ?? []) as Fragment[]) {
    const current = calls.get(frag.index) ?? { id: '', name: '', arguments: '' };
    current.id ||= frag.id ?? '';
    current.name += frag.function?.name ?? '';
    current.arguments += frag.function?.arguments ?? '';
    calls.set(frag.index, current);
  }
}
console.log([...calls.values()]);
```

## When a model cannot use tools

If the selected model cannot honour tools, the gateway refuses the request with
`capability_unsupported` (HTTP 400) rather than silently dropping them. Pick a model whose
`capabilities` include tools (`ur.models.list({ capability: 'tools' })`).

```ts
import UltraRouter, { isUltraRouterError } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
try {
  await ur.chat.completions.create({
    model: 'example/no-tools',
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }],
    tools: [{ type: 'function', function: { name: 'noop', parameters: { type: 'object' } } }],
  });
} catch (err) {
  if (isUltraRouterError(err, 'capability_unsupported')) console.log('choose a tool-capable model');
  else throw err;
}
```

## Related

- [Chat completions](./chat-completions.md) · [Structured outputs](./structured-outputs.md)
- [Streaming](./streaming.md) · [Models](./models.md)
- Runnable example: [`examples/tools.ts`](../examples/tools.ts)

<!-- file: docs/structured-outputs.md -->

# Structured outputs

Ask the model for JSON with `response_format`. There are two modes:

- `{ type: 'json_schema', json_schema: { name, schema, strict? } }` — JSON that matches your JSON
  Schema. Prefer this whenever the model supports it.
- `{ type: 'json_object' }` — any valid JSON object (describe the shape in the prompt).

The content still arrives as a string in `choices[0].message.content`; parse it with `JSON.parse`.

## JSON Schema

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });

const schema = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    sentiment: { type: 'string', enum: ['positive', 'neutral', 'negative'] },
    score: { type: 'number' },
    topics: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['sentiment', 'score', 'topics'],
  additionalProperties: false,
};

const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Review: "Fast delivery, but the box was damaged."' }],
  response_format: { type: 'json_schema', json_schema: { name: 'review', strict: true, schema } },
});

const review = JSON.parse(res.choices[0]?.message.content ?? '{}') as {
  sentiment: string;
  score: number;
  topics: string[];
};
console.log(review.sentiment, review.score, review.topics);
```

`strict: true` asks providers that support strict schema adherence to enforce it. Even so, parse
defensively and validate the result if a wrong shape would be costly.

## JSON object mode

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  messages: [
    { role: 'system', content: 'Reply with a JSON object: {"result": string}.' },
    { role: 'user', content: 'Translate "thank you" to Spanish.' },
  ],
  response_format: { type: 'json_object' },
});
console.log(JSON.parse(res.choices[0]?.message.content ?? '{}'));
```

## When a model cannot honour the format

A model that does not support `json_schema` is refused with `capability_unsupported` before
dispatch; the gateway never silently downgrades `json_schema` to plain text. Choose a model whose
capabilities include it:

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const models = await ur.models.list({ capability: 'json_schema' });
console.log(models.data.map((m) => m.id));
```

## Tips

- Keep schemas small and explicit: `required` on every property you need,
  `additionalProperties: false`, and `enum` for closed sets.
- Ask for a summary field rather than free text inside a large object.
- Combine with a `call_type` so the gateway can evaluate requests of the same kind together.

## Related

- [Chat completions](./chat-completions.md) · [Tools](./tools.md) · [Models](./models.md)
- Runnable example: [`examples/structured-output.ts`](../examples/structured-output.ts)

<!-- file: docs/embeddings.md -->

# Embeddings

`ur.embeddings.create(params, options?)` turns text into vectors (`POST /v1/embeddings`). The
request and response follow the OpenAI embeddings shape; the response also carries the `ur` block.

## Embed a batch

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

const res = await ur.embeddings.create({
  model: 'openai/text-embedding-3-small',
  input: ['How do I reset my password?', 'Password reset steps', 'Shipping to Canada'],
});

for (const item of res.data) {
  const vector = item.embedding as number[];
  console.log(item.index, vector.length);
}
console.log(res.usage.total_tokens, res.ur.request_id);
```

`data[i].index` matches the position of the input. Send many inputs in one call rather than one
call per input.

## Parameters

| Parameter          | Type                  | Notes                                                                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`            | `string`              | An embedding model id. Optional when the client has `defaultModel`.       |
| `input`            | `string \| string[]`  | One text or a batch.                                                      |
| `dimensions`       | `number`              | Output dimensions, for models that support shortening.                    |
| `encoding_format`  | `'float' \| 'base64'` | `float` (default) returns `number[]`; `base64` returns a base64 string.   |
| `call_type`        | `string`              | A stable slug for this kind of request.                                   |
| `ur`               | `UrRequestOptions`    | Per-request controls (`trace_id`, `tags`, `max_cost_usd`, `artifact`, …). |
| `bench`            | Bench tag             | Tag the call for a Bench suite.                                           |
| `user`, `metadata` |                       | An end-user id; free-form metadata.                                       |

The `ur` response block on embeddings has no `compression` field.

## Base64 output

Base64 encoding returns little-endian float32 values packed into a string, which is smaller to
transfer. Decode it like this:

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const res = await ur.embeddings.create({
  model: 'openai/text-embedding-3-small',
  input: 'decode me',
  encoding_format: 'base64',
});

const b64 = res.data[0]?.embedding as string;
const bytes = Buffer.from(b64, 'base64');
const vector = new Float32Array(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, bytes.byteLength / 4);
console.log(vector.length);
```

## Shorter vectors

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const res = await ur.embeddings.create({
  model: 'openai/text-embedding-3-small',
  input: 'compact vector',
  dimensions: 16,
});
console.log((res.data[0]?.embedding as number[]).length);
```

## Related

- [Models](./models.md) — find embedding models with `ur.models.list({ capability: 'embeddings' })`.
- [Configuration](./configuration.md) · [Errors](./errors.md)
- Runnable example: [`examples/embeddings.ts`](../examples/embeddings.ts)

<!-- file: docs/models.md -->

# Models

The model catalog is what your API key can use through the gateway: each model's id, context
window, capabilities, pricing and provenance. Model ids are provider-prefixed
(`openai/gpt-5.2-mini`); the ids in these docs are illustrative, and the catalog you see depends on
your gateway and workspace.

## List models

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const { data } = await ur.models.list();

for (const m of data) {
  console.log(m.id, m.context_length, m.pricing.input_usd_per_1m, m.pricing.output_usd_per_1m);
}
```

Filter by provider or capability (`GET /v1/models?provider=…&capability=…`):

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const openai = await ur.models.list({ provider: 'openai' });
const toolCapable = await ur.models.list({ capability: 'tools' });
console.log(
  openai.data.length,
  toolCapable.data.map((m) => m.id),
);
```

### Model fields

| Field                  | Meaning                                                                                |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`, `name`           | The provider-prefixed id and a display name.                                           |
| `provider`             | The provider slug.                                                                     |
| `context_length`       | The context window in tokens, or `null` when unknown.                                  |
| `capabilities`         | Capability flags such as `tools`, `json_schema`, `vision`, `embeddings`.               |
| `pricing`              | Per 1M tokens, in USD (`input_usd_per_1m`, `output_usd_per_1m`) and integer micro-USD. |
| `active`               | Whether the model is currently served.                                                 |
| `origin_jurisdiction`  | The developing lab's jurisdiction (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), or `unknown`.                  |
| `hosting_jurisdiction` | Where this offer runs, or `unknown`.                                                   |
| `hosting_region`       | The provider-published serving region, or `null`.                                      |
| `weights`              | `open`, `closed` or `unknown`.                                                         |
| `workspace_custom`     | `true` for a model served by one of your workspace's custom providers.                 |

A model with no price cannot be called: the gateway refuses it with `model_unpriced`. See
[errors](./errors.md#model_unpriced).

## Retrieve one model

`ur.models.retrieve(id)` returns one logical model with every provider offer that serves it
(`GET /v1/models/{id}`). The SDK keeps the `/` in the id when it builds the URL.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const model = await ur.models.retrieve('openai/gpt-5.2-mini');

console.log(model.id, model.context_length, model.weights, model.origin_jurisdiction);
for (const offer of model.offers) {
  console.log(offer.provider, offer.hosting_jurisdiction, offer.hosting_region);
}
```

An unknown id rejects with `not_found` (HTTP 404).

## Related

- [Chat completions](./chat-completions.md) · [Embeddings](./embeddings.md)
- [Errors](./errors.md)
- Runnable example: [`examples/models.ts`](../examples/models.ts)

<!-- file: docs/errors.md -->

# Errors

Every method of the client rejects with an `UltraRouterError` (or its subclass `ModelUnpricedError`)
when something goes wrong. The error carries a stable string `code`, the HTTP `status`, the
gateway `requestId` and a `retryable` flag, so your code branches on a string instead of guessing
from a status or parsing a message.

## The error object

| Field          | Type                  | Meaning                                                                                            |
| -------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`         | `string`              | A stable code: one of the gateway codes below, or a client-side code (`connection`, `timeout`, …). |
| `status`       | `number`              | The HTTP status of the failed response; `0` when no response arrived (network error, timeout).     |
| `requestId`    | `string \| undefined` | The gateway correlation id (`req_…`). Quote it when you report a problem.                          |
| `retryable`    | `boolean`             | Whether the same request may be retried as-is. The SDK only auto-retries retryable errors.         |
| `providerCode` | `string \| undefined` | The raw upstream provider error code, when a provider produced the failure.                        |
| `message`      | `string`              | A human-readable explanation. Do not branch on it; branch on `code`.                               |

```ts
import UltraRouter, { UltraRouterError } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

try {
  await ur.chat.completions.create({
    model: 'example/unpriced-model',
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }],
  });
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof UltraRouterError) {
    console.log(err.code); // 'model_unpriced'
    console.log(err.status); // 403
    console.log(err.retryable); // false
    console.log(err.requestId); // 'req_…'
  } else {
    throw err;
  }
}
```

## Narrowing helpers

- `err instanceof UltraRouterError` — any SDK error.
- `err instanceof ModelUnpricedError` — the typed `model_unpriced` refusal.
- `isUltraRouterError(err, code?)` — a type guard, optionally narrowed to one code.
- `isGatewayErrorCode(code)` — whether a string is one of the stable gateway codes.
- `GATEWAY_ERROR_CODES` — every gateway code; `GATEWAY_ERROR_TAXONOMY[code]` — its canonical
  `status` and `retryable` flag.

```ts
import UltraRouter, { GATEWAY_ERROR_TAXONOMY, isUltraRouterError } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

async function ask(question: string): Promise<string> {
  try {
    const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
      model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
      messages: [{ role: 'user', content: question }],
    });
    return res.choices[0]?.message.content ?? '';
  } catch (err) {
    if (isUltraRouterError(err, 'context_length')) return 'That question is too long.';
    if (isUltraRouterError(err, 'rate_limited')) return 'Busy, try again shortly.';
    throw err;
  }
}

console.log(await ask('What is 2 + 2?'));
console.log(GATEWAY_ERROR_TAXONOMY.rate_limited); // { status: 429, retryable: true }
```

## `model_unpriced`

The gateway refuses a call to a model it has no price for, because a call it cannot cost would be
invisible to spend caps and budgets. The refusal happens before dispatch: nothing reaches a
provider and nothing is billed.

- HTTP status `403`, code `model_unpriced`.
- Surfaces as `ModelUnpricedError` (a subclass of `UltraRouterError`); `retryable` is always `false`.
- **Never retried**, whatever the status or the envelope says.
- Fix it by choosing a priced model (`ur.models.list()` shows pricing), or by declaring pricing on
  the custom provider that serves the model.

```ts
import UltraRouter, { ModelUnpricedError } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

try {
  await ur.chat.completions.create({
    model: 'example/unpriced-model',
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }],
  });
} catch (err) {
  if (!(err instanceof ModelUnpricedError)) throw err;
  const priced = await ur.models.list();
  console.log(`unpriced model refused; ${String(priced.data.length)} priced models available`);
}
```

## Gateway error codes

These are the codes the gateway returns (`GATEWAY_ERROR_CODES`). "Retried" means the SDK retries
the request automatically (up to `maxRetries`, see
[retries, timeouts and idempotency](./retries-timeouts-idempotency.md)).

| Code                             | HTTP | Retried | What it means and what to do                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------- | ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invalid_request`                | 400  | no      | The body or parameters are invalid, or an option is unsupported. Fix the request.                                     |
| `manifest_invalid`               | 400  | no      | A declared `ur.manifest` is malformed (for example overlapping ranges). Rebuild it with `toWire()`.                   |
| `manifest_mismatch`              | 400  | no      | A declared `ur.manifest` hash does not match the bytes sent. Recompute the manifest over the exact messages you send. |
| `authentication`                 | 401  | no      | Missing or invalid API key. Check `ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY` / `apiKey`.                                                   |
| `permission`                     | 403  | no      | The key lacks the scope the route needs (for example `config:write`). Use a key with that scope.                      |
| `not_found`                      | 404  | no      | Unknown model, request or resource. Check the id.                                                                     |
| `model_denied_by_policy`         | 403  | no      | Your workspace model policy forbids this model. Choose another model or change the policy.                            |
| `model_unpriced`                 | 403  | no      | The model has no price, so the call is refused before dispatch. Use a priced model. Raised as `ModelUnpricedError`.   |
| `capability_unsupported`         | 400  | no      | The model cannot honour a requested capability (tools, `json_schema`, vision, reasoning). Choose a model that can.    |
| `prompt_variables_missing`       | 400  | no      | The active hosted prompt needs `{{variables}}` you did not send in `ur.prompt_vars`. The message names them.          |
| `conflict`                       | 409  | no      | An idempotent write collided with a different payload under the same key. Use a new id for a new event.               |
| `rate_limited`                   | 429  | yes     | A rate limit was hit. Retried with backoff, honouring `Retry-After`.                                                  |
| `spend_cap_exceeded`             | 402  | no      | The key or workspace spend cap for the period is reached.                                                             |
| `max_cost_exceeded`              | 402  | no      | The estimated cost of this one call exceeds `ur.max_cost_usd`. Raise the cap or shrink the request.                   |
| `atomic_spend_guard_unavailable` | 503  | no      | Live Bench execution is not available on this deployment. Dry runs still work.                                        |
| `provider_unavailable`           | 502  | yes     | The upstream provider is unreachable or failed. Retried; add fallbacks with `models: [...]`.                          |
| `provider_timeout`               | 504  | yes     | The upstream provider exceeded its deadline. Retried.                                                                 |
| `content_filtered`               | 400  | no      | The provider refused the content (moderation or safety).                                                              |
| `context_length`                 | 400  | no      | The prompt plus the requested completion exceeds the model's context window. Shorten it or pick a larger model.       |
| `cancelled`                      | 499  | no      | The client disconnected before the request completed.                                                                 |
| `internal`                       | 500  | no      | An unexpected gateway failure. Report it with the `requestId`.                                                        |

The SDK treats the taxonomy as authoritative: a code marked "no" is never retried, even when it
arrives with a 5xx status or an envelope that says otherwise.

## Client-side codes

| Code               | Status          | Retried          | When                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | --------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `connection`       | `0`             | yes              | The request never got a response (DNS failure, connection refused or reset).                                       |
| `timeout`          | `0`             | no               | The total `timeout` elapsed (it covers every retry).                                                               |
| `aborted`          | `0`             | no               | Your `AbortSignal` fired.                                                                                          |
| `invalid_response` | response status | no               | The response could not be used (for example a non-JSON body where JSON was expected).                              |
| `invalid_request`  | `0`             | no               | The SDK refused before sending (for example a missing path parameter in `request()`).                              |
| `authentication`   | `0`             | no               | The constructor found no API key (`apiKey`, `ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY` or `UR_API_KEY`).                                |
| `http_<status>`    | that status     | 408, 429 and 5xx | A component in front of the gateway (a proxy, a load balancer) answered without the gateway's JSON error envelope. |

## Errors during a stream

A streamed response can fail after it has started. The gateway sends an `event: error` frame and
the `for await` loop throws an `UltraRouterError` with the code from that frame (its `status` is
`0`, because the HTTP status was already 200). Once a stream has opened it is never retried; a
streaming request that fails with a retryable response before it opens is retried like any other
request. See [streaming](./streaming.md).

## Errors from `useLearned().record()` and the outcome queue

`ur.outcomes.record()` does not throw for a delivery failure: it resolves a receipt whose `status`
is `delivered`, `queued` (the outcome is unknown, or the event was not refused; it stays in the
durable queue) or `rejected` (the gateway definitively refused the event, with the `error`
attached). It throws only `OutcomeStoreError`, when its store cannot persist the event.

`isDefinitiveRejection(err)` is the rule: a 4xx other than 401, 403, 408 and 429 whose body is a
well-formed gateway envelope (`err.envelope` is set) with `"retryable": false` and a code from
`EVENT_REJECTION_CODES` (`invalid_request`, `not_found`, `conflict`) at its taxonomy status. An error
decoded from anything else (an HTML page from a proxy, an empty body, another JSON shape) has
`err.envelope === undefined`, and the event stays queued. See [outcomes](./outcomes.md).

## Related

- [Retries, timeouts and idempotency](./retries-timeouts-idempotency.md)
- [Troubleshooting](./troubleshooting.md)
- [API reference](./api/sdk.md)

<!-- file: docs/retries-timeouts-idempotency.md -->

# Retries, timeouts and idempotency

The SDK's transport retries transient failures automatically, bounds every call with a total
timeout, lets you cancel with an `AbortSignal`, and attaches an idempotency key to writes so a
retried POST can never execute twice. All of it is configurable per client and per call.

## Defaults

| Setting         | Default                          | Set it with                                                    |
| --------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Retries         | `2` (3 attempts)                 | `new UltraRouter({ maxRetries })` or per call `{ maxRetries }` |
| Total timeout   | `600000` ms                      | `new UltraRouter({ timeout })` or per call `{ timeout }`       |
| Abort           | none                             | per call `{ signal }`                                          |
| Idempotency key | generated per non-streaming POST | per call `{ idempotencyKey }`                                  |

The constants are exported as `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES` and `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`.

## What is retried

A failure is retried only when it is **retryable**, there are retries left, and there is time left
before the total timeout (a stream only before it opens; see [Streaming retries](#streaming-retries)):

- Gateway errors marked retryable in the taxonomy: `rate_limited` (429), `provider_unavailable`
  (502) and `provider_timeout` (504). See the [error table](./errors.md#gateway-error-codes).
- Network failures with no response (`connection`).
- A response without the gateway's JSON error envelope (for example from a proxy) with status
  408, 429 or 5xx.

Everything else is surfaced immediately. The gateway's explicit flag wins over the status class:

- An error body that says `"retryable": false` is never retried, even with a 5xx status. A 5xx with
  no such flag (or no error body at all) is retried.
- A gateway code marked non-retryable in the taxonomy is never retried, whatever its status or
  flag: `model_unpriced`, `invalid_request`, `internal`, `atomic_spend_guard_unavailable` and the
  rest fail on the first attempt.

## Backoff

Between attempts the SDK waits with jittered exponential backoff: about 250–500 ms before the first
retry, doubling per attempt, capped at 8 s. When the response carries a `Retry-After` header (in
seconds or as an HTTP date) the SDK waits that long instead (up to 32 s). A wait never extends past
the total timeout.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

// Retry up to 4 times, but give up after 20 seconds in total.
const ur = new UltraRouter({ maxRetries: 4, timeout: 20_000 });

// `example/flaky` fails once with provider_unavailable on the local mock gateway, then succeeds.
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'example/flaky',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hello' }],
});
console.log(res.choices[0]?.message.content);
```

## Per-call overrides

Every method takes request options as its last argument. They override the client settings for
that call only.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

// A latency-sensitive call: no retries, 5-second budget.
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create(
  { model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Quick yes or no?' }] },
  { maxRetries: 0, timeout: 5_000, headers: { 'x-request-source': 'checkout' } },
);
console.log(res.ur.request_id);
```

| Option           | Type                     | Effect                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `signal`         | `AbortSignal`            | Abort the call and any pending retry.                       |
| `timeout`        | `number` (ms)            | Total time for this call, retries and backoff included.     |
| `maxRetries`     | `number`                 | Retries for this call.                                      |
| `headers`        | `Record<string, string>` | Extra headers; they win over the client's `defaultHeaders`. |
| `idempotencyKey` | `string`                 | Use this idempotency key instead of a generated one.        |

## Timeouts and cancellation

The timeout is a deadline for the whole call: every attempt, the backoff between them, and reading
the response body. When it passes, the call rejects with an `UltraRouterError` whose code is
`timeout`; when your `AbortSignal` fires, the code is `aborted`. Both have status `0` and neither
is retried. A response whose body arrives slower than the deadline fails with `timeout` while it is
being read, and aborting after the headers arrived still cancels the body read.

For a stream the deadline covers the whole stream, until the last chunk: a stream that stalls or
runs past it makes the `for await` loop throw `timeout` (and aborting your signal mid-stream makes
it throw `aborted`). Set `timeout` per call to the longest generation you accept — the default is
10 minutes. Leaving the loop early (`break`) or finishing it releases the timer and the signal.

```ts
import UltraRouter, { isUltraRouterError } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const controller = new AbortController();
controller.abort(); // for example, the user navigated away before the call was made

try {
  await ur.models.list(undefined, { signal: controller.signal });
} catch (err) {
  if (isUltraRouterError(err, 'aborted')) console.log('aborted:', err.message);
  else throw err;
}
```

## Idempotency

Every non-streaming `POST` carries an `Idempotency-Key` header. The SDK generates one random UUID
per call and reuses it on every retry of that call, so when a response is lost after the gateway
already acted, the retry replays the original result instead of acting twice.

Pass your own key when the same logical operation can be submitted more than once by your
application (for example after your process restarts):

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const orderId = 'order-4711';

const res = await ur.chat.completions.create(
  {
    model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: `Draft a receipt for ${orderId}` }],
  },
  { idempotencyKey: `receipt-${orderId}` },
);
console.log(res.id);
```

Outcome events have an extra layer: the durable outcome queue fixes each event's
`source_event_id` and `observed_at` before the first send, so a retry is recorded by the gateway as
a duplicate, never as a second event. See [outcomes](./outcomes.md).

## Streaming retries

A request with `stream: true` carries no idempotency key. If the gateway answers it with a
retryable error before the stream opens (for example `rate_limited` or `provider_unavailable`),
nothing was generated, so the SDK retries it like any other request. It is never retried after a
network failure (the request may already have reached the gateway) or once the stream has opened;
a failure mid-stream makes the `for await` loop throw. Retry at the application level if your use
case allows it. See [streaming](./streaming.md).

## Related

- [Errors](./errors.md)
- [Configuration](./configuration.md)
- [Testing your app](./testing.md)

<!-- file: docs/openai-compatibility.md -->

# OpenAI compatibility

The gateway speaks the OpenAI HTTP API under `/v1`, and this SDK mirrors the `openai` client's
shape. You can adopt ultrarouter in three ways, from least to most change:

1. Keep the official `openai` client and point it at the gateway (`asOpenAI`).
2. Keep the `openai` client and set `baseURL` / `apiKey` yourself.
3. Switch to `UltraRouter`, whose `chat.completions.create`, `embeddings.create` and `models.list`
   have the same shape, plus typed access to the `ur` response block and the ultrarouter
   resources.

`openai` is not a dependency of this SDK; install it yourself if you use it.

## `asOpenAI(OpenAI)`: a ready `openai` client

Pass the `OpenAI` constructor and get an instance configured with the gateway URL (with `/v1`), your
API key and the client's default headers:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'openai';
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const openai = new UltraRouter().asOpenAI(OpenAI);

const res = await openai.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello through the openai client' }],
});
console.log(res.choices[0]?.message.content);
```

## `asOpenAI()`: just the configuration

Without an argument, `asOpenAI()` returns `{ baseURL, apiKey, defaultHeaders? }` so you can add your
own options:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'openai';
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const config = new UltraRouter().asOpenAI();
const openai = new OpenAI({ ...config, timeout: 20_000, maxRetries: 1 });

const stream = await openai.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  stream: true,
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Stream through openai' }],
});
for await (const chunk of stream) process.stdout.write(chunk.choices[0]?.delta.content ?? '');
process.stdout.write('\n');
```

`ur.ur.asOpenAI` is the same method.

## Configuring `openai` directly

No SDK needed: use the gateway URL with `/v1` and your ultrarouter key.

```ts
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const openai = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: `${process.env.ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL}/v1`, // your gateway, e.g. http://localhost:8080
  apiKey: process.env.ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY,
});
const models = await openai.models.list();
console.log(models.data.map((m) => m.id));
```

## What carries over

| From the `UltraRouter` client           | Carried by `asOpenAI()`?                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `baseURL`, `apiKey`                     | Yes (`/v1` is appended).                                                                                  |
| `defaultHeaders`                        | Yes.                                                                                                      |
| The `bench` capture tag                 | Yes — its `X-UR-Bench-*` headers are part of the default headers (a per-request `trace` function is not). |
| `defaultModel`, `defaults`, `autopilot` | No — they are applied by `UltraRouter` when it builds a request. Set them per call in `openai`.           |
| Retries, timeout                        | No — the `openai` client has its own `maxRetries` and `timeout`.                                          |

The ultrarouter request fields (`call_type`, `router`, `compression`, `provider`, `models`, `ur`)
are extra body fields; with the `openai` client you can still send them (the `openai` client
passes unknown body fields through in JavaScript, and TypeScript users can cast), and the response
still carries the `ur` block at runtime.

## Surface mapping

| `openai`                                    | `UltraRouter`                               | Notes                                             |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `chat.completions.create(params)`           | `chat.completions.create(params, options?)` | Same params; adds `ur` and extensions.            |
| `chat.completions.create({ stream: true })` | same                                        | Async iterable of chunks.                         |
| `embeddings.create(params)`                 | `embeddings.create(params, options?)`       | Same params.                                      |
| `models.list()`                             | `models.list(query?, options?)`             | Adds `provider` / `capability` filters.           |
| `models.retrieve(id)`                       | `models.retrieve(id, options?)`             | Returns the model with its provider offers.       |
| `new OpenAI({ baseURL, apiKey })`           | `new UltraRouter({ baseURL, apiKey })`      | `baseURL` here has no `/v1`.                      |
| `OpenAI.APIError`                           | `UltraRouterError`                          | Stable `code` strings; see [errors](./errors.md). |

Differences to keep in mind:

- `UltraRouter`'s `baseURL` is the gateway origin **without** `/v1`; `openai`'s includes it.
  `asOpenAI()` adds it for you.
- Errors are `UltraRouterError` with a gateway `code` rather than OpenAI's error classes.
- Model ids are provider-prefixed (`openai/gpt-5.2-mini`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`).
- The Assistants, Files, Images and Audio APIs are not part of this SDK. The OpenAI Responses API
  (and the Anthropic Messages API) are reachable as [native passthrough](./passthrough.md) — point
  the official `openai` / `@anthropic-ai/sdk` clients at the gateway.

## Related

- [Chat completions](./chat-completions.md) · [Streaming](./streaming.md)
- [Configuration](./configuration.md)
- Runnable example: [`examples/openai-drop-in.ts`](../examples/openai-drop-in.ts)

<!-- file: docs/passthrough.md -->

# Native passthrough: the official OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs through your gateway

The gateway speaks two more vendor APIs natively: the OpenAI Responses API at `POST /v1/responses`
and the Anthropic Messages API at `POST /v1/messages`. Point the official `openai` and
`@anthropic-ai/sdk` clients at your gateway, change only the base URL and the key, and each request
body is forwarded to the provider unchanged, metered, and returned untouched.

Unlike `chat.completions.create` and `embeddings.create`, these two surfaces are **opaque
passthrough**: the gateway does no routing, no compression, no model remapping and no field
injection. The body you send is the body the provider receives; the body the provider returns is the
body you get back (`stream: true` forwards the upstream SSE bytes verbatim). The gateway only meters,
caps and captures the call.

The intended client for these surfaces is the official vendor SDK pointed at the gateway, not a typed
method in this SDK. This SDK's own `ur.request()` reaches them too, for raw REST access.

## Two environment variables and the key

| Surface            | Base URL (env)                                 | Key (env)                              |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| OpenAI Responses   | `OPENAI_BASE_URL=<your gateway>/v1`            | `OPENAI_API_KEY=<your ur_sk_… key>`    |
| Anthropic Messages | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<your gateway>` (no `/v1`) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<your ur_sk_… key>` |

Use your ultrarouter key (`ur_sk_test_…` or `ur_sk_live_…`), not a provider key — the platform or
BYOK provider key is injected server-side and your key is never forwarded upstream. The OpenAI client
sends the key as an `Authorization: Bearer` token; the Anthropic client sends it as `x-api-key`. The
gateway accepts the ultrarouter key either way on `/v1/messages`.

<!-- doctest: skip — installs the official SDKs from the npm registry and only sets environment variables -->

```bash
npm install openai @anthropic-ai/sdk

# Point each official client at your gateway (use https://gateway.example.com for a remote one).
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="http://localhost:8080/v1"
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://localhost:8080"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="ur_sk_test_your_key"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="ur_sk_test_your_key"
```

## The ultrarouter extension headers

The ultrarouter extensions ride **request headers**, so the provider body stays untouched:

| Request header    | Meaning                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `X-UR-Call-Type`  | The stage/call-type slug this call belongs to.                                           |
| `X-UR-Trace`      | A JSON object `{"run","case","stage","attempt"}` that ties the call to a run and a case. |
| `X-UR-Timeout-Ms` | The total timeout, clamped to 1 s–600 s (default 300 s).                                 |

Every (non-streaming) response carries two **response headers**:

| Response header       | Meaning                                               |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `X-UR-Request-Id`     | The ultrarouter request id (`req_…`) for this call.   |
| `X-UR-Cost-Micro-USD` | The booked cost of the call, an integer in micro-USD. |

## The OpenAI Responses API through your gateway

With `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` set as above, the official client needs no other change.
Pass the ultrarouter headers per request, and read the two response headers with the client's
`.withResponse()`:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'openai';

// Reads OPENAI_BASE_URL (your gateway + /v1) and OPENAI_API_KEY (your ur_sk_… key).
const openai = new OpenAI();

const { data, response } = await openai.responses
  .create(
    { model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini', input: 'Give me one word for "fast".' },
    {
      headers: {
        'X-UR-Call-Type': 'drafting',
        'X-UR-Trace': JSON.stringify({ run: 'run_1', case: 'case_1', stage: 'draft', attempt: 1 }),
        'X-UR-Timeout-Ms': '30000',
      },
    },
  )
  .withResponse();

console.log(data.output_text);
console.log('request id:', response.headers.get('X-UR-Request-Id'));
console.log('cost (micro-USD):', response.headers.get('X-UR-Cost-Micro-USD'));
```

## The Anthropic Messages API through your gateway

`@anthropic-ai/sdk` is not a dependency of this SDK; install it in your app. With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`
and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, the official client is unchanged — the ultrarouter key goes in
`x-api-key` (the Anthropic default) and the same ultrarouter headers tag the call:

<!-- doctest: skip — the official @anthropic-ai/sdk is not a dependency of this SDK; install it in your app -->

```ts
import Anthropic from '@anthropic-ai/sdk';

// Reads ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (your gateway, no /v1) and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (your ur_sk_… key).
const anthropic = new Anthropic();

const { data, response } = await anthropic.messages
  .create(
    {
      model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6',
      max_tokens: 64,
      messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Give me one word for "fast".' }],
    },
    {
      headers: {
        'X-UR-Call-Type': 'drafting',
        'X-UR-Trace': JSON.stringify({ run: 'run_1', case: 'case_1', stage: 'draft', attempt: 1 }),
        'X-UR-Timeout-Ms': '30000',
      },
    },
  )
  .withResponse();

const block = data.content[0];
console.log(block?.type === 'text' ? block.text : '');
console.log('request id:', response.headers.get('X-UR-Request-Id'));
console.log('cost (micro-USD):', response.headers.get('X-UR-Cost-Micro-USD'));
```

## Reaching the passthrough from this SDK with `ur.request()`

You can also call both operations from this SDK with [`ur.request()`](./typed-requests.md). The body
is an opaque passthrough object, so it is typed as `{ model: string }` and extra provider fields are
passed with a cast; the result is the provider's response body. `ur.request()` resolves the body
only — read the `X-UR-Request-Id` / `X-UR-Cost-Micro-USD` response headers with the official clients'
`.withResponse()` (above) or a custom `fetch`.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

// POST /v1/responses — the OpenAI Responses body is forwarded to OpenAI unchanged.
const res = (await ur.request('post', '/v1/responses', {
  body: { model: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini', input: 'Give me one word for "fast".' } as never,
  headers: { 'X-UR-Call-Type': 'drafting' },
})) as unknown as { object: string; model: string; status: string };
console.log(res.object, res.status, res.model);

// POST /v1/messages — the Anthropic Messages body is forwarded to Anthropic unchanged.
const msg = (await ur.request('post', '/v1/messages', {
  body: {
    model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6',
    max_tokens: 64,
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Give me one word for "fast".' }],
  } as never,
  headers: { 'X-UR-Call-Type': 'drafting' },
})) as unknown as { type: string; model: string; stop_reason: string };
console.log(msg.type, msg.model, msg.stop_reason);
```
