  `chat.completions` / `embeddings` surfaces this SDK mirrors.
- [Typed requests](./typed-requests.md) — `ur.request()` for any operation in the OpenAPI document.
- [API coverage](./api-coverage.md) — every gateway operation and how this SDK reaches it.

<!-- file: docs/call-types.md -->

# Call types

A **call type** is a stable name for one kind of request your application makes, for example
`support-reply` or `invoice-triage`. The gateway groups traffic by call type, and each call type
carries its own configuration (model pin, routing, compression, fallbacks, provider preferences),
its eval history, its hosted prompt versions and its learning settings.

You attach a request to a call type with `call_type` (per call) or `defaults.callType` (per client).
Everything on this page lives under `ur.ur.callTypes` and needs an API key with the `config:read`
scope (reads) or `config:write` scope (writes).

- [Tag requests with a call type](#tag-requests-with-a-call-type)
- [Create, read and update](#create-read-and-update)
- [Configuration fields](#configuration-fields)
- [Evals and recommendations](#evals-and-recommendations)
- [Hosted prompts](#hosted-prompts)
- [Verified memory](#verified-memory)
- [Autopilot readiness](#autopilot-readiness)

## Tag requests with a call type

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

// Every call from this client is attributed to `support-reply` unless a call overrides it.
const ur = new UltraRouter({
  defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini',
  defaults: { callType: 'support-reply' },
});

const reply = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Where is my order 4821?' }],
});
console.log(reply.ur.call_type, reply.ur.request_id);

// A per-call value wins over the client default.
const triage = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  call_type: 'invoice-triage',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Is invoice 77 a duplicate?' }],
});
console.log(triage.ur.call_type);
```

Use a slug that names the _task_, not the model or the prompt version: the slug is what evals,
recommendations and learning are keyed on, so it should stay the same when you change models.

## Create, read and update

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

// Create (needs `config:write`). The initial config is optional.
const created = await ur.ur.callTypes.create({
  slug: 'support-reply',
  config: { model_pin: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini', fallbacks: ['anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6'] },
});
console.log(created.id, created.current_config_version);

// Read one by slug or by `ct_*` id, or list them all.
const one = await ur.ur.callTypes.get('support-reply');
const all = await ur.ur.callTypes.list();
console.log(one.slug, all.data.length);

// Update = append a new immutable config version. Omitted fields keep their value; an explicit
// `null` clears a field.
const updated = await ur.ur.callTypes.update('support-reply', {
  compression_mode: 'semantic_safe',
});
console.log(updated.current_config_version, updated.config?.compression_mode);
```

Config versions are immutable: every `update` appends a version and repoints the call type to it, so
you can always tell which configuration served a request. The gateway picks up a change within one
config-cache window (a few seconds).

## Configuration fields

`CallTypeConfigBody` (sent to `create({ config })` and `update(id, config)`):

| Field                      | Type                                                                                                                              | Meaning                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model_pin`                | `string \| null`                                                                                                                  | Pin a model for this call type. `null` clears the pin.                                                                                        |
| `router_mode`              | `'pinned' \| 'auto' \| 'candidates' \| 'off' \| null`                                                                             | How the router treats this call type.                                                                                                         |
| `compression_mode`         | `'off' \| 'semantic_safe' \| 'adaptive' \| null`                                                                                  | Compression tier. `off` (the default) never rewrites what the model sees. `lossless` / `auto` are deprecated legacy aliases that still parse. |
| `fallbacks`                | `string[] \| null`                                                                                                                | Ordered fallback model ids.                                                                                                                   |
| `provider_prefs`           | `object \| null`                                                                                                                  | Provider preferences (same shape as the per-request `provider`).                                                                              |
| `learned_context_delivery` | `'gateway_inject_after_stable_prefix' \| 'off'`                                                                                   | Whether the gateway injects learned context on proxied requests, or leaves it to callers using [`useLearned`](./preflight.md).                |
| `case_precedents_enabled`  | `boolean`                                                                                                                         | Serve per-request case precedents (verified past cases similar to the current input) into the learned slot. Default `false`.                  |
| `self_improve_mode`        | `'off' \| 'assist' \| 'autopilot'`                                                                                                | `off` records outcomes only; `assist` proposes tested improvements to your inbox; `autopilot` adopts passed improvements within guardrails.   |
| `self_improve_guardrails`  | `{ max_cost_per_success_micro_usd?: number \| null; surfaces?: ('knowledge_injection' \| 'model_routing' \| 'hosted_prompt')[] }` | The cost budget per successful task (integer micro-USD) and the surfaces autopilot may change.                                                |

The returned `CallType` carries the active `config` (a `CallTypeConfigVersion`), the
`current_config_version` number and the read-only lifecycle fields (`lifecycle_state`,
`lifecycle_reason`, `lifecycle_transitioned_at`). The lifecycle state is informational: it never
changes how a request is served by itself.

## Evals and recommendations

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

// Trigger an eval run. `mode: 'task'` evaluates whole traces instead of single requests.
const trigger = await ur.ur.callTypes.enqueueEval('support-reply', { mode: 'request' });
if (trigger.enqueued) {
  console.log('enqueued run', trigger.run_id, 'candidates:', trigger.candidate_count);
} else {
  // A documented no-op, e.g. `no_golden_set`, `no_candidates` or `deduped`.
  console.log('not enqueued:', trigger.reason, trigger.prior_run_id ?? '');
}

// Every run with its candidates and the immutable run spec it executed.
const runs = await ur.ur.callTypes.listEvals('support-reply');
for (const run of runs.data) {
  console.log(
    run.id,
    run.status,
    run.candidates.map((c) => `${c.model}:${String(c.passed)}`),
  );
}

// The eval-backed model recommendations for the call type.
const recommendations = await ur.ur.callTypes.recommendations('support-reply');
console.log(Object.keys(recommendations));
```

`enqueueEval` resolves to one of two shapes, discriminated by `enqueued`:

| `enqueued` | Fields                                                            | Meaning                                                                                      |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `true`     | `run_id`, `candidate_count`                                       | A run was queued.                                                                            |
| `false`    | `reason`, `deduped`, optional `prior_run_id`, `trigger`, `status` | Nothing new was queued. A deduplicated trigger names the run it joined so you can follow it. |

The recommendations route does not publish a response schema yet, so `recommendations()` returns
an open object (`Record<string, unknown>`). Inspect it rather than relying on fixed fields.

## Hosted prompts

A hosted prompt moves a call type's system prompt out of your code and into versioned, immutable
gateway records. Versions are created inactive; activating one makes it the call type's prompt, and
activating an older version is the rollback.

```ts
import UltraRouter, { renderPrompt } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

// 1. Create a version (inactive until activated).
const v = await ur.ur.callTypes.prompts.create('support-reply', {
  template: 'You are a support assistant for {{brand}}. Answer in {{language}}.',
  variables: [
    { name: 'brand', required: true },
    { name: 'language', required: false },
  ],
});
console.log('created version', v.version, v.content_sha256);

// 2. Activate it. With `gateway_apply: true` the gateway renders the template and sends it as the
//    leading system instruction on proxied requests; with `false` you fetch and render it yourself.
const pointer = await ur.ur.callTypes.prompts.activate('support-reply', v.version, {
  gateway_apply: false,
});
console.log('active version', pointer.active_version, 'config version', pointer.config_version);

// 3. Render it client-side with the same fail-closed rule the gateway applies.
const active = await ur.getPrompt('support-reply');
const template = active ?? {
  template: v.template,
  variables: v.variables.map((x) => ({ name: x.name, required: x.required ?? false })),
};
console.log(renderPrompt(template, { brand: 'Acme' }));

// List every version, read one, or go back to the code-owned prompt.
const versions = await ur.ur.callTypes.prompts.list('support-reply');
console.log(versions.data.length, versions.active_version);
await ur.ur.callTypes.prompts.deactivate('support-reply');
```

| Method                                           | Route                                                 | Notes                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `prompts.list(callTypeId)`                       | `GET /v1/call-types/{id}/prompts`                     | Every version plus `active_version` and `gateway_apply`.                                                                                                             |
| `prompts.create(callTypeId, params)`             | `POST /v1/call-types/{id}/prompts`                    | `{ template, variables? }`. Creates an inactive version.                                                                                                             |
| `prompts.get(callTypeId, version)`               | `GET /v1/call-types/{id}/prompts/{version}`           | One immutable version.                                                                                                                                               |
| `prompts.activate(callTypeId, version, params?)` | `POST /v1/call-types/{id}/prompts/{version}/activate` | `{ gateway_apply?: boolean }`. Writes a new config version.                                                                                                          |
| `prompts.deactivate(callTypeId)`                 | `POST /v1/call-types/{id}/prompts/deactivate`         | Back to the code-owned prompt (your messages pass through untouched).                                                                                                |
| `prompts.proposal(callTypeId)`                   | `GET /v1/call-types/{id}/prompts/proposal`            | A suggested first version derived from consented captured traffic, or `available: false` with a named `reason`. Nothing is applied until you create and activate it. |

When the gateway applies a hosted prompt (`gateway_apply: true`), pass the variable values per
request in `ur.prompt_vars`. A missing required variable is refused before dispatch with the
`prompt_variables_missing` error; it is never replaced by an empty string.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  call_type: 'support-reply',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Where is my order?' }],
  ur: { prompt_vars: { brand: 'Acme', language: 'English' } },
});
console.log(res.choices[0]?.message.content);
```

See [Preflight and learned context](./preflight.md#hosted-prompts-rendered-client-side) for
`getPrompt` and `renderPrompt` in detail.

## Verified memory

Verified memory lets the gateway answer a request directly from the call type's verified past
outcomes, without calling a model, when a calibrated similarity rule says it is safe. It applies only
to label-style call types (one instruction plus one text user turn) and only to requests whose
meaning the stored answer captures; every other request reaches the model as usual. An answered
request carries `ur.verified_memory` in its response and `ur.routing.engine === 'verified_memory'`.

Enabling it requires an authorisation on your workspace that ultrarouter grants; without it
`enable` fails with a `permission` error. Disabling is always allowed and is the kill switch.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

const status = await ur.ur.callTypes.verifiedMemory.get('ticket-classifier');
console.log(
  'enabled:',
  status.enabled,
  'servable:',
  status.servable?.ok,
  status.servable?.reason ?? '',
);

// Calibrates against the declared precision target and enables only if an operating point clears it.
const enabled = await ur.ur.callTypes.verifiedMemory.enable('ticket-classifier', {
  target_precision: 0.97,
});
console.log('enabled:', enabled.enabled, enabled.reason ?? '');

// The kill switch: every request reaches the model again within one config-cache window.
const disabled = await ur.ur.callTypes.verifiedMemory.disable('ticket-classifier');
console.log('changed:', disabled.changed);
```

| Method                                      | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get(callTypeId)`                           | `enabled`, the frozen `setting`, `servable` (`{ ok, reason }`, or `null` when nothing is enabled), the live pool status and `post_pin` accounting (answered / correct / wrong / unknown).                                    |
| `enable(callTypeId, { target_precision? })` | `enabled: true` with the frozen setting, or `enabled: false` with a named `reason` (for example `pool_empty` or `calibration_below_target`) and nothing written. `target_precision` is between 0.8 and 0.999 (default 0.95). |
| `disable(callTypeId)`                       | Appends a config version with memory off. `changed: false` when it was already off (idempotent).                                                                                                                             |

The calibration figures are an in-sample read of the chosen operating point, not an independent
precision guarantee; `post_pin` reports what happened after enabling.

## Autopilot readiness

`ur.ur.autopilot.status()` reads the read-only readiness rollup (`GET /v1/audit/readiness`): the call
types the gateway inferred, their lifecycle state, evidence gaps and what each one needs next. It never
changes how anything is served.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ autopilot: 'audit' });
const readiness = await ur.ur.autopilot.status();
console.log(ur.ur.autopilot.mode, readiness.state, readiness.total_requests);
for (const ct of readiness.call_types) {
  console.log(ct.slug, ct.lifecycle_state, ct.evidence_gaps.join(', '));
}
```

The `autopilot` client option (`audit`, `recommend`, `auto`) is described in
[Configuration](./configuration.md).

## Pitfalls

- **Renaming a slug starts a new history.** Evals, recommendations and learning are keyed on the call
  type; keep slugs stable across model and prompt changes.
- **`update` is a partial update.** Send only the fields you want to change; `null` clears a field.
- **Activation is not instant everywhere.** A config change becomes visible to the gateway within one
  config-cache window (a few seconds), not mid-request.
- **Hosted prompt variables fail closed.** A required variable that is missing is an error, never a
  blank.

## Related

- [Preflight and learned context](./preflight.md) — `getPrompt`, `renderPrompt`, `useLearned`
- [Feedback, generation stats and key info](./feedback-and-generation.md)
- [Outcomes and artifacts](./outcomes.md)
- [Bench](./bench.md) — evaluate a call type against a pinned baseline in CI
- API reference: [`CallTypesResource`](./api/sdk.md#calltypesresource),
  [`HostedPromptsResource`](./api/sdk.md#hostedpromptsresource),
  [`VerifiedMemoryResource`](./api/sdk.md#verifiedmemoryresource)

<!-- file: docs/feedback-and-generation.md -->

# Feedback, generation stats and key info

Three small reads and writes that work on any request the gateway served:

- **Feedback** (`ur.ur.requests.feedback`) attaches a thumbs up or down, tags and a comment to a
  request. It is the quickest human signal you can send, and evals consume it.
- **Generation stats** (`ur.ur.generation.get`) describe one served request after the fact: tokens,
  cost, latency, the routing decision and any outcomes bound to it (compatible with the OpenRouter
  `/generation` route).
- **Key info** (`ur.ur.key.get`) describes the API key the client is using: its scopes, caps and
  usage this period.

All three use the request id from the `ur` block of a response (`res.ur.request_id`, a `req_…`
string). Feedback and generation need the `gateway:invoke` scope, which every gateway key has.

## Rate a request

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });

const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarise our refund policy in one sentence.' }],
});

// Thumbs down with tags and a comment. `rating` is 1 (good) or -1 (bad).
const feedback = await ur.ur.requests.feedback(res.ur.request_id, {
  rating: -1,
  tags: ['too_long', 'missed_exception'],
  comment: 'Did not mention the 30-day window.',
});
console.log(feedback.id, feedback.rating, feedback.tags);
```

| Field     | Type       | Notes                              |
| --------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `rating`  | `1 \| -1`  | Required.                          |
| `tags`    | `string[]` | Optional, up to 32 free-form tags. |
| `comment` | `string`   | Optional, up to 4,000 characters.  |

The route wraps the stored row in `{ feedback: … }`; the SDK unwraps it and resolves a bare
`Feedback` (`id`, `request_id`, `rating`, `tags`, `comment`, `created_at`). The wire type
`FeedbackEnvelope` is exported for raw-REST callers.

Feedback is a per-request signal. To record what actually happened to the thing your application
produced (accepted, edited, resolved), use [outcomes](./outcomes.md) instead.

## Read generation stats

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({ messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }] });

const stats = await ur.ur.generation.get(res.ur.request_id);
console.log(stats.status, stats.model_requested, '→', stats.model_served);
console.log('tokens', stats.tokens.input, stats.tokens.output, 'cached', stats.tokens.cached);
console.log('cost', stats.cost.total_usd, 'USD /', stats.cost.total_micro_usd, 'micro-USD');
console.log(
  'latency',
  stats.timing.latency_ms,
  'ms; time to first byte',
  stats.timing.ttfb_ms,
  'ms',
);
```

| Field                                           | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `status`                                        | `ok`, `error` or `cancelled`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `model_requested` / `model_served` / `provider` | What you asked for and what actually served it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `error_class`                                   | The error class of a failed request, or `null`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `tokens`                                        | `{ input, output, cached, total }`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `cost`                                          | `{ total_micro_usd, total_usd, cost_basis }`. Money is an integer number of micro-USD in the API; `cost_basis` says what the figure rests on: `priced` (the catalog price), `derived` (a dated snapshot priced from its base), `unpriced` (no catalog price, metered at 0 — the gateway refuses such models unless explicitly configured to allow them), `verified_memory` (no provider call), or `null`. |
| `timing`                                        | `{ ttfb_ms, latency_ms }` (either may be `null`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `routing_decision`                              | The routing trail (open object).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `compression`                                   | What compression did (open object).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `contract_digest`                               | A digest of the declared contract (schema, tools, tool choice, response format), or `null`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `outcomes`                                      | Outcome events bound to this request (channel, kind, observed time, value — never a body).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `exposure`                                      | The experiment arm and epoch stamped before dispatch (`null` fields when none).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `lever`                                         | What learned context was served (ids and numbers only) or why none was.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `byok`                                          | Whether your own provider key served it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

An unknown or foreign request id is a `not_found` error.

## Inspect the API key

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const key = await ur.ur.key.get();
console.log(key.name, key.mode, key.workspace_id);
console.log('scopes:', key.scopes.join(', '));
console.log('spent this period (micro-USD):', key.usage.key_spent_micro_usd);
console.log('caps:', key.limits.rps_limit, key.limits.spend_cap_micro_usd);
```

`mode` is `live` or `test` (`ur_sk_live_…` / `ur_sk_test_…`). `scopes` tells you which routes the key
may call: for example `gateway:invoke` (chat, embeddings, models, preflight, feedback),
`config:read` / `config:write` (call types, Bench freeze), `outcomes:write` (artifacts, outcomes,
imports, reviewer events) and `bench:run` (Bench runs). A call outside the key's scopes fails with a
`permission` error. When the workspace has learning usage, `flywheel` reports the usage quantities
and caps for the current period.

`key.get()` is a cheap way to check that a key and base URL work at startup.

- [Outcomes and artifacts](./outcomes.md) — richer signals than a thumbs up
- [Configuration](./configuration.md) — API keys and base URLs
- API reference: [`UrNamespace`](./api/sdk.md#urnamespace), [`GenerationStats`](./api/sdk.md#generationstats),
  [`KeyInfo`](./api/sdk.md#keyinfo)

<!-- file: docs/outcomes.md -->

# Outcomes and artifacts

Model calls are only half of the story; what matters is what happened to the thing your application
produced. Was the draft accepted, edited or rejected? Did the forecast come true? Did the extracted
JSON pass validation? The outcome ledger records those facts so routing, evals and learning can use
them.

Three concepts:

| Concept           | What it is                                                                                                                     | SDK                   |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| **Artifact type** | A named kind of artifact plus its _objective_: what "it worked" means for it. Declared once, versioned.                        | `ur.ur.artifactTypes` |
| **Artifact**      | One unit of value your application produced (a reply, a forecast, an extraction), keyed by your own `key`.                     | `ur.ur.artifacts`     |
| **Outcome event** | A typed fact about an artifact (or one of its claims, or a request): channel + kind + an optional numeric value. Never a body. | `ur.ur.outcomes`      |

Everything on this page needs an API key with the `outcomes:write` scope.

- [Quick start: `withArtifact`](#quick-start-withartifact)
- [Declare an artifact type](#declare-an-artifact-type)
- [Create and read artifacts](#create-and-read-artifacts)
- [Record outcomes](#record-outcomes)
- [The durable queue](#the-durable-queue)
- [Record the approved final](#record-the-approved-final)
- [Batch and pending claims](#batch-and-pending-claims)

## Quick start: `withArtifact`

`withArtifact(key, fn)` binds every chat and embeddings call inside `fn` to one artifact (it sets
`ur.artifact = key` on each request), gives you `record` and `final` for that artifact, and flushes
the outcome queue when `fn` finishes, whether it returns or throws.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });

const draft = await ur.withArtifact('ticket-4821-reply', async (scope) => {
  const res = await scope.chat.completions.create({
    messages: [
      { role: 'user', content: 'Draft a reply to ticket 4821: the parcel arrived damaged.' },
    ],
  });
  const text = 'choices' in res ? (res.choices[0]?.message.content ?? '') : '';

  // A mechanical fact you can check in code right away.
  await scope.record({ channel: 'mechanical', kind: 'schema_valid' });
  return text;
});
console.log(draft);
```

The artifact is created lazily, on the first `record` or `final`, so a scope that only chats makes
no extra request.

## Declare an artifact type

Declare the objective before you record outcomes, so every artifact of that type is judged against
the same definition. Versions are append-only: an unchanged upsert is a no-op that returns the
existing version, so it is safe to call at startup.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

const type = await ur.ur.artifactTypes.upsert({
  name: 'support-reply',
  archetype: 'draft',
  objective: {
    metric: 'acceptance_rate',
    direction: 'higher_is_better',
    unit: 'ratio',
    source: 'support agent review',
    window: 'P7D',
    resolution_criteria: 'The agent sends the draft with no more than light edits.',
  },
});
console.log(type.name, 'objective version', type.version);
```

| Objective field       | Meaning                                                                                                        |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `metric`              | `claim_resolution`, `oracle_delta`, `correction_rate`, `acceptance_rate`, `engagement_rate` or `task_success`. |
| `direction`           | Which direction is good, e.g. `higher_is_better` or `true_is_good`.                                            |
| `unit`                | The unit of the metric, e.g. `ratio`, `boolean`, `usd`.                                                        |
| `source`              | Where the resolving signal comes from (a reviewer, a system, an oracle name).                                  |
| `window`              | How long resolution may take, as an ISO-8601 duration (`P7D`, `P12M`).                                         |
| `resolution_criteria` | How it resolves, in words. Keep it free of personal data.                                                      |
| `predicate_id`        | Optional machine predicate: `equals`, `within_tolerance`, `ge`, `le`, `resolved_by_source`.                    |
| `alternatives`        | Optional named alternatives for computable comparisons.                                                        |

`archetype` is one of `forecast`, `recommendation`, `draft`, `extraction`, `answer` or `action`.

## Create and read artifacts

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

// Upsert by your own key. Optional: an artifact type, declared claims, the requests it came from.
const artifact = await ur.ur.artifacts.create({
  key: 'forecast-2026-q3-revenue',
  archetype: 'forecast',
  claims: [
    {
      key: 'q3-revenue',
      claim_type: 'numeric_forecast',
      statement: 'Q3 revenue lands between 1.1M and 1.3M',
      resolves_by: '2026-10-15T00:00:00.000Z',
      stated_confidence: 0.7,
    },
  ],
});
console.log(artifact.id, artifact.lifecycle, artifact.claims.length);

const again = await ur.ur.artifacts.get(artifact.id);
console.log(again.key, again.current_version);

// Keyset pagination: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`; it is null on the last page.
const first = await ur.ur.artifacts.list({ archetype: 'forecast', limit: 50 });
for (const a of first.data) console.log(a.key);
if (first.next_cursor !== null) {
  const second = await ur.ur.artifacts.list({
    archetype: 'forecast',
    limit: 50,
    cursor: first.next_cursor,
  });
  console.log('next page:', second.data.length);
}
```

`create` fields: `key` (required, unique per workspace), `archetype` (default `answer`),
`artifact_type` (pins that type's current objective version), `claims[]`, `request_ids[]` (the
requests it was assembled from), `occurred_at`, `situation_facets` (labels and values only), and the
grant fields `grant_id` + `attestation` used by [`useLearned`](./preflight.md). A request already
grouped into another artifact is a `conflict` error. Artifacts never carry bodies; reads return
metadata only.

You can also bind a request to an artifact as it is served, without `withArtifact`, by sending
`ur: { artifact: '<key>' }` on the chat or embeddings call. The response echoes the bound id in
`res.ur.artifact_id`.

## Record outcomes

An outcome event has a `channel` (closed vocabulary) and a `kind` (a closed vocabulary per channel):

| Channel      | Use it for                                   | Example kinds                                             |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mechanical` | Facts your code checks immediately           | `schema_valid`, `tool_success`, `tool_error`              |
| `correction` | A human's judgement of a draft               | `accepted_unchanged`, `edited`, `rejected`, `regenerated` |
| `behavioral` | What a user did                              | `accepted`                                                |
| `resolution` | Whether a claim came true                    | `resolved_true`, `resolved_false`                         |
| `computable` | A score your own evaluator computed          | `scored`                                                  |
| `proxy`      | Indirect signals that rank but are not proof |                                                           |

The gateway refuses a kind it does not know with a named reason. Optional fields: `value` (numbers
and diff statistics only), `confidence`, `claim_id` / `claim_key` (target a claim instead of the
artifact), `artifact_version`, `observed_at` (when it happened in your world; defaults to now),
`source_event_id` (your idempotency id), `supersedes_event_id`, `evidence_hash`,
`tool_error_class` (for `mechanical:tool_error`) and `alternative_id`.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ defaultModel: 'openai/gpt-5.2-mini' });
const artifact = await ur.ur.artifacts.create({
  key: 'forecast-2026-q3-revenue',
  archetype: 'forecast',
});

// On an artifact (a bare string is an artifact id) …
const receipt = await ur.ur.outcomes.record(artifact.id, {
  channel: 'resolution',
  kind: 'resolved_true',
  claim_key: 'q3-revenue',
  observed_at: '2026-10-14T12:00:00.000Z',
});
console.log(receipt.status, receipt.entryId);

// … or on a request (it lands on the request's artifact, created if needed).
const res = await ur.chat.completions.create({
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Extract the total.' }],
});
await ur.ur.outcomes.record(
  { request: res.ur.request_id },
  { channel: 'mechanical', kind: 'schema_valid' },
);

// `recordOutcome` is the same method at the top level.
await ur.recordOutcome(artifact.id, {
  channel: 'computable',
  kind: 'scored',
  value: { score: 0.82 },
});
```

The fields `source`, `producer`, `learning_use` and `latency_class` are assigned by the gateway from
your credential and the event; the input type does not have them, so you cannot set them by accident.

## The durable queue

`ur.outcomes.record` never throws for a delivery failure and never loses an event:

1. It finalizes the event: `observed_at` and `source_event_id` are fixed now.
2. It **persists** the event to the client's outcome store **before** the first network send.
3. It tries one delivery and resolves a receipt.
4. Unless the gateway definitively refused the event, it stays queued; `flush()` replays it
   **verbatim**, with the **same `Idempotency-Key`** (`ur-outcome-<entry id>`, derived from the
   persisted entry, so it is the same after a process restart too).

Because a replay is byte-identical (same `observed_at`, same `source_event_id`, same key), the
gateway sees it as a `duplicate` of the event it may already have, never as a second, conflicting
event.

Only a **definitive refusal of the event** drops it (`isDefinitiveRejection(err)` is the exact
rule). All of these must hold:

- the answer is a 4xx other than 401, 403, 408 and 429 — those four keep the event whatever their
  body, code or `retryable` flag says;
- its body is a well-formed gateway error envelope, `{ "error": { "code", "message", "request_id",
"retryable" } }` with every field present and typed (the error's `envelope` property);
- the code refuses the event itself — `invalid_request` (400), `not_found` (404) or `conflict`
  (409), the list in `EVENT_REJECTION_CODES` — at the status the taxonomy assigns it;
- the envelope says `"retryable": false`.

Everything else keeps the event queued, because its outcome is unknown or the event itself was not
refused: a timeout (including the SDK's own deadline), a cancellation, a connection failure, any
401 / 403 / 408 / 429 or 5xx answer, an answer without the envelope (an HTML 400 from a proxy, an
empty or unreadable body), a code about something else (a spend cap, a permission) or one this SDK
does not know, and a success the contract does not describe. Fix what the error names (for example
the key) and flush again.

| Receipt `status` | Meaning                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `delivered`      | The gateway recorded it; `result` holds the server row (`accepted` or `duplicate`).                 |
| `queued`         | The outcome is unknown, or the event was not refused; it stays in the store for the next `flush()`. |
| `rejected`       | The gateway definitively refused the event; `error` explains it. It is removed from the queue.      |

The one thing `record()` does throw is an `OutcomeStoreError`: a store that cannot persist the
event (for example a `FileOutcomeStore` whose file is unreadable) cannot honour "persist first".

The default store, `MemoryOutcomeStore`, lives in the process. For events that must survive a
restart, pass a `FileOutcomeStore` (Node.js only; `node:fs` is loaded lazily, so edge bundles are
unaffected) or your own `OutcomeStore`. `FileOutcomeStore` rewrites its JSON file atomically (a
temporary file with mode `0600`, then a rename). It starts empty **only** when the file does not
exist: a file that cannot be read, is not valid JSON or does not hold a list of entries makes every
operation throw `OutcomeStoreError`, and the file is never overwritten, so the events in it can be
recovered. Point each client at its own file.

```ts
import UltraRouter, { FileOutcomeStore } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({ outcomeStore: new FileOutcomeStore('.ur-outcomes.json') });

await ur.ur.outcomes.record({ request: 'req_123' }, { channel: 'behavioral', kind: 'accepted' });

// Drain anything still queued, for example before the process exits.
const report = await ur.ur.outcomes.flush();
console.log(`delivered=${report.delivered} rejected=${report.rejected} pending=${report.pending}`);
```

`OutcomeStore` is a small interface (`append`, `update`, `remove`, `list`, sync or async); implement
it over Redis, a database table or anything durable. `append` must not resolve before the entry is
durable. A store may be shared by several clients (for example an in-memory store handed to two
clients): each client delivers with its own configuration — the client that calls `flush()` sends
every queued event with its own key, base URL, headers, timeout and retries — and every replay
keeps the event's identity and Idempotency-Key, so delivering the same entry twice is a harmless
`duplicate`. The reviewer adapter uses the same store interface (`reviewerStore`); see
[Reviewer decisions](./reviewer.md).

## Record the approved final

When a human edits and approves a draft, record the final on the artifact. What you may send depends
on whether your workspace granted **corrections consent**:

- **Without consent** (the default): send statistics only. `diffStats(draft, final)` computes them
  locally; the draft and the final never leave your process. The row is stored as metadata only.
- **With consent**: send `{ final, draft? }` and the gateway stores the final (encrypted) and computes
  the statistics itself. Sending a body without consent is rejected with `invalid_request`.

```ts
import UltraRouter, { diffStats } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const artifact = await ur.ur.artifacts.create({ key: 'ticket-4821-reply', archetype: 'draft' });

const draft = 'Sorry your parcel arrived damaged. We will send a replacement.';
const final =
  'Sorry your parcel arrived damaged. We will ship a replacement today, free of charge.';

const stats = diffStats(draft, final); // pure, local: lengths, edit ratio, changed spans, sha256
const version = await ur.ur.artifacts.final(artifact.id, {
  diff_stats: stats,
  final_hash: stats.final_hash,
});
console.log(
  stats.edit_ratio.toFixed(3),
  stats.changed_spans,
  version.stored,
  version.client_computed,
);
```

`diffStats` returns `{ edit_ratio, changed_spans, lengths: { draft, final }, final_hash }`.
`edit_ratio` is 0 for identical text and 1 for no shared content; on very large inputs it degrades
conservatively (it can only report more change, never less).

## Batch and pending claims

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

// Up to 1,000 events per call, each keyed by request_id, artifact_id or artifact_key.
const batch = await ur.ur.outcomes.batch([
  { artifact_key: 'ticket-4821-reply', channel: 'correction', kind: 'edited' },
  { artifact_key: 'ticket-4822-reply', channel: 'correction', kind: 'accepted_unchanged' },
  { request_id: 'req_123', channel: 'mechanical', kind: 'schema_valid' },
]);
console.log(`accepted=${batch.accepted} duplicate=${batch.duplicate} rejected=${batch.rejected}`);

// Claims still waiting for a resolution (`overdue` = past `resolves_by`).
const pending = await ur.ur.outcomes.pending({ state: 'overdue', limit: 20 });
for (const claim of pending.data)
  console.log(claim.artifact_key, claim.claim_key, claim.resolves_by);
```

`batch` is a direct call (not queued): each row gets its own verdict (`accepted`, `duplicate`,
`conflict` or `rejected` with a `reason`). It is the right tool for backfills. `pending` is keyset
paginated (`cursor` / `next_cursor`) and filterable by `state`, `since` and `archetype`.

## Pitfalls

- **Never put text in `value`.** Outcomes carry numbers, ids and hashes only; use `artifacts.final`
  (with consent) for text.
- **Call `flush()` before exit** when you use `record` outside `withArtifact`, or use a
  `FileOutcomeStore` so queued events survive a restart.
- **Reuse `source_event_id` only for the same event.** The same id with a different payload is a
  `conflict`.
- **`observed_at` is when it happened**, not when you send it; it must not be earlier than the
  artifact's `occurred_at`.

## Related

- [Reviewer decisions](./reviewer.md) — the signed adapter for approve / reject / edit decisions
- [History imports](./imports.md) — bring past traffic and outcomes in bulk
- [Learning status](./learning.md) — what the ledger is doing with your outcomes
- [Preflight and learned context](./preflight.md) — record outcomes that quote an exposure grant
- API reference: [`ArtifactsResource`](./api/sdk.md#artifactsresource),
  [`OutcomesResource`](./api/sdk.md#outcomesresource), [`diffStats`](./api/sdk.md#diffstats)

<!-- file: docs/reviewer.md -->

# Reviewer decisions

Your people already approve, reject or edit what the model drafts: in a review queue, an admin page,
a ticket workflow. Those decisions are among the most valuable signals you have. The reviewer adapter
(`ur.ur.reviewer`) is the supported way to send them to ultrarouter: a small, signed, idempotent HTTP
contract plus a typed client with a durable local queue.

There are no third-party connectors here, and none are promised. You call the adapter from wherever
your reviewer clicks _Approve_, or post the documented HTTP request from any language.

Needs an API key with the `outcomes:write` scope.

- [What an event is](#what-an-event-is)
- [What each decision becomes](#what-each-decision-becomes)
- [The TypeScript path](#the-typescript-path)
- [Prove the integration first](#prove-the-integration-first)
- [Backfill historical decisions](#backfill-historical-decisions)
- [Dead letters and repair](#dead-letters-and-repair)
- [The raw HTTP recipe](#the-raw-http-recipe)
- [Responses and refusals](#responses-and-refusals)

## What an event is

| Field              | Required | What it is                                                                                                        |
| ------------------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `event_id`         | yes      | **Your** review system's stable id. It is the idempotency key: re-sending it is free.                             |
| `artifact_key`     | one of   | The stable key of the reviewed artifact (for example `invoice:4711`).                                             |
| `artifact_id`      | one of   | Or its ultrarouter id. Send exactly one of the two.                                                               |
| `artifact_version` | yes      | The exact draft version the person read.                                                                          |
| `decision`         | yes      | `approved`, `approved_with_edits`, `rejected` or `regenerated`.                                                   |
| `effective_at`     | yes      | When the decision happened in your world (ISO 8601), not when you upload it.                                      |
| `reviewer_id`      | no       | An opaque reviewer id. Never a name or an email address.                                                          |
| `final`            | no       | The approved final: `{ hash, diff_stats }`, or `{ draft, text }` when your workspace granted corrections consent. |

There is deliberately no `learning_use`, `source` or `producer` field: provenance comes from the API
key you authenticate with, and how an event may be used is derived by the gateway. The TypeScript
type (`ReviewerEvent`) does not have those fields, and the HTTP route refuses them.

## What each decision becomes

`ur.ur.reviewer.setup()` returns this mapping as a machine-readable preview before you send anything:

| Your decision         | Recorded as                     |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `approved`            | `correction:accepted_unchanged` |
| `approved_with_edits` | `correction:edited`             |
| `rejected`            | `correction:rejected`           |
| `regenerated`         | `correction:regenerated`        |

A reviewer's verdict is a **correction** about the draft. It is evidence about the draft, not proof
that the final is correct: nothing here resolves a claim or produces a quality score on its own.

## The TypeScript path

```ts
import UltraRouter, { FileOutcomeStore, type QueuedReviewerEvent } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter({
  // Queued decisions survive a restart and are replayed verbatim by flush().
  reviewerStore: new FileOutcomeStore<QueuedReviewerEvent>('.ur-reviewer-queue.json'),
});

// Call this from your "Approve" handler. Nothing touches the network until flush().
await ur.ur.reviewer.record(
  {
    event_id: 'rv-1001', // your id: the idempotency key
    artifact_key: 'invoice:4711',
    artifact_version: 3, // the exact draft the person read
    decision: 'approved_with_edits',
    effective_at: '2026-09-14T10:00:00.000Z',
    reviewer_id: 'reviewer-7',
    final: { hash: 'sha256:9f2c', diff_stats: { edit_ratio: 0.08, changed_spans: 1 } },
  },
  { reviewerSystem: 'my-review-queue' },
);

const report = await ur.ur.reviewer.flush();
console.log(
  `accepted=${report.accepted} duplicate=${report.duplicate} dead-lettered=${report.deadLettered}`,
  `dropped=${report.dropped} still-queued=${report.pending}`,
);
```

| Method                                          | What it does                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `setup()`                                       | The mapping preview, the signature recipe, your consent state and the required scope.   |
| `test(scenario?)`                               | Runs a guided scenario end to end: `happy` (default), `replay` or `version_mismatch`.   |
| `record(event, { backfill?, reviewerSystem? })` | Persists one decision locally and resolves its queue-entry id. Sends nothing.           |
| `flush()`                                       | Sends everything queued, in batches, signed. Resolves a `ReviewerFlushReport`.          |
| `send(events, opts?)`                           | Sends a signed batch immediately, bypassing the queue.                                  |
| `deadLetters()`                                 | Events refused with a repairable reason, still held locally.                            |
| `repair(entry, { repinToCurrentVersion? })`     | Re-drives one dead letter. On success it is cleared locally.                            |
| `health()`                                      | Integration health: last success, counts, backfill progress and the next repair action. |

The queue uses the same `OutcomeStore` interface as outcomes (see [the durable queue](./outcomes.md#the-durable-queue));
the default is in memory. Events leave the queue only through the gateway's per-event verdicts, and
only through a verdict that validates (`reviewerVerdictAction`): an object with the event's
`event_id` and a defined `status`, plus, for a refusal, a string `reason` and a boolean `repairable`.
`flush()` never throws for an individual refusal — `accepted` / `duplicate` remove the event, a
`rejected` / `unsupported` verdict with `repairable: true` becomes a dead letter, and one with
`repairable: false` is dropped and counted. A missing or malformed verdict (a refusal without
`repairable` or `reason`, an unknown status) keeps the event queued. A failure whose outcome is unknown (a timeout, a cancellation, a connection failure, a 408,
429 or 5xx answer, a success without a list of verdicts) leaves the whole batch queued and ends the
flush quietly. Any other 4xx answer for the whole request (a 401 or 403, a bad signature, an invalid
batch, an HTML error page from a proxy) also leaves the batch queued, and is thrown as an
`UltraRouterError`. A failed delivery never removes an event.

## Prove the integration first

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();

const setup = await ur.ur.reviewer.setup();
console.log(
  `${setup.signature.algorithm}: ${setup.signature.header} + ${setup.signature.timestamp_header}`,
);
for (const row of setup.mapping) console.log(`${row.decision} → ${row.channel}:${row.kind}`);

// The happy path: a test artifact plus an edited final, joined.
const happy = await ur.ur.reviewer.test('happy');
console.log(happy.result.status, happy.excluded_from_learning, happy.excluded_from_invoicing);

// A replay of the same event id is a visible no-op.
const replay = await ur.ur.reviewer.test('replay');
console.log('replay →', replay.result.status);

const health = await ur.ur.reviewer.health();
console.log('next action:', health.next_repair.action, '-', health.next_repair.detail);
```

Test scenarios run against a reserved artifact. Their data never enters learning or invoicing, and
the response says so field by field (`excluded_from_learning`, `excluded_from_invoicing`).

## Backfill historical decisions

Send months of history as a declared backfill so progress is attributable and a resumed run never
double-counts. You declare `{ id, total }` on each event and `complete: true` on the last one;
completion is never inferred from counts.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
const history = [
  {
    id: 'rv-0001',
    key: 'invoice:4711',
    version: 1,
    verdict: 'approved_with_edits',
    at: '2026-08-02T09:12:00Z',
  },
  {
    id: 'rv-0002',
    key: 'invoice:4712',
    version: 1,
    verdict: 'rejected',
    at: '2026-08-02T11:40:00Z',
  },
] as const;

for (const [i, row] of history.entries()) {
  await ur.ur.reviewer.record(
    {
      event_id: row.id,
      artifact_key: row.key,
      artifact_version: row.version,
      decision: row.verdict,
      effective_at: row.at, // the historical instant, not "now"
    },
    {
      reviewerSystem: 'my-review-queue',
      backfill: {
        id: 'reviews-2026-08',
        total: history.length,
        ...(i === history.length - 1 ? { complete: true } : {}),
      },
    },
  );
}
const report = await ur.ur.reviewer.flush();
console.log(`accepted=${report.accepted} duplicate=${report.duplicate} pending=${report.pending}`);
```

Re-running a backfill is safe: every `event_id` you already sent comes back as `duplicate`.

## Dead letters and repair

Some refusals can be fixed: the artifact does not exist yet, or the draft moved on since the person
read it. The client keeps those events locally as **dead letters** (the gateway keeps receipts, not
your payloads), so you can repair them instead of losing a person's decision.

```ts
import UltraRouter from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const ur = new UltraRouter();
await ur.ur.reviewer.flush();

for (const entry of await ur.ur.reviewer.deadLetters()) {
  console.log(entry.event.event_id, entry.dead_letter?.reason);
  // Opt in to re-pinning to the current draft version; it is never done silently.
  const repaired = await ur.ur.reviewer.repair(entry, { repinToCurrentVersion: true });
  console.log('repaired →', repaired.result?.status ?? 'still failing');
}
```

`repinToCurrentVersion` is opt-in on purpose: "the person reviewed draft 2" and "draft 3 exists now"
are different facts.

## The raw HTTP recipe

If your review system posts webhooks rather than running Node.js, this is the whole contract.

**Sign the request.** The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `"<unix-seconds>.<exact request body>"`,
hex-encoded, prefixed `sha256=`, keyed by **your ultrarouter API key**, sent as
`X-UR-Reviewer-Signature` together with `X-UR-Reviewer-Timestamp`:

<!-- doctest: skip — a raw HTTP call to the hosted gateway with your own key; `test/reviewer.test.ts` verifies the same signature recipe -->

```bash
UR_API_KEY=ur_sk_live_your_key
BODY='{"reviewer_system":"my-review-queue","events":[{"event_id":"rv-1001","artifact_key":"invoice:4711","artifact_version":3,"decision":"approved_with_edits","effective_at":"2026-09-14T10:00:00Z","final":{"hash":"sha256:9f2c","diff_stats":{"edit_ratio":0.08,"changed_spans":1}}}]}'
TS=$(date +%s)
SIG="sha256=$(printf '%s.%s' "$TS" "$BODY" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$UR_API_KEY" -hex | sed 's/^.* //')"

curl -sS https://gateway.example.com/v1/flywheel/reviewer/events \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $UR_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "X-UR-Reviewer-Timestamp: $TS" \
  -H "X-UR-Reviewer-Signature: $SIG" \
  --data-raw "$BODY"
```

The timestamp is part of the signed bytes, so a captured request cannot be replayed with a fresh
timestamp. The accepted clock skew is `setup.signature.tolerance_seconds`; the durable `event_id`
idempotency is the real replay defence and never expires.

The same three steps in Python:

```python
import hashlib, hmac, json, time, requests

body = json.dumps({"events": [event]}, separators=(",", ":"))
ts = str(int(time.time()))
sig = "sha256=" + hmac.new(api_key.encode(), f"{ts}.{body}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
requests.post(
    f"{base_url}/v1/flywheel/reviewer/events",
    data=body,  # the exact bytes you signed, not a re-serialized dict
    headers={
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "X-UR-Reviewer-Timestamp": ts,
        "X-UR-Reviewer-Signature": sig,
    },
)
```

Sign the bytes you send. If your HTTP library re-serializes the payload, the signature will not match
and the delivery is refused. The SDK exports the same recipe (`signReviewerPayload`,
`reviewerSignatureHeaders`) so you can check another implementation against it:

```ts
import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto';
import { signReviewerPayload } from '@ultrarouter/sdk';

const body = JSON.stringify({ events: [] });
const sdk = await signReviewerPayload('ur_sk_test_key', '1767225600', body);
const manual = `sha256=${createHmac('sha256', 'ur_sk_test_key').update(`1767225600.${body}`).digest('hex')}`;
console.log(sdk === manual); // true
```

Repair and health over plain HTTP are `POST /v1/flywheel/reviewer/repair` with
`{ "event": { … the original event … }, "repin_to_current_version": true }` and
`GET /v1/flywheel/reviewer/health` (both with the `Authorization` header only).

## Responses and refusals

The events route answers `200` with a verdict per event:

| `status`      | Meaning                                                                              |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `accepted`    | Recorded. `reason` may carry markers such as `delayed` or `final_absent`.            |
| `duplicate`   | You sent this `event_id` before. A visible no-op, not a second row and not an error. |
| `rejected`    | Refused with a named reason. `repairable: true` means re-driving it can fix it.      |
| `unsupported` | This deployment cannot act on it (for example no store for a consented final).       |

Named refusals you may see:

| Reason                                 | What to do                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unmatched_artifact_key`               | The artifact does not exist yet. Create it, then re-send the same event id.  |
| `wrong_tenant_artifact_id`             | That artifact id is not in this workspace. Check which key you used.         |
| `version_mismatch:claimed=2,current=3` | The draft moved on. Repair with the version the person actually read.        |
| `final_body_without_consent`           | Enable corrections consent, or send `diff_stats` + `hash` instead of a body. |
| `ledger_conflict`                      | That `event_id` was used for a different payload. Use a new id.              |

Request-level failures are `403` responses naming `missing_signature`, `stale_signature` or
`invalid_signature`. They fail closed: nothing is written.

## What the contract will not do

- Invent an artifact for a review that points at something it never saw.
- Treat a missing final as an approved one (an `approved` decision without a final is recorded and
  marked `final_absent`).
- Store a final body without corrections consent.
- Attach a decision to a draft version other than the one the person read; it is held for repair.
- Let you set `learning_use`, `source` or `producer`.

  [`examples/reviewer/backfill.ts`](../examples/reviewer/backfill.ts)
